adalbert_of_prague_bishop.label: The painting
adalbert_of_prague_bishop.text: Saint Adalbert, a wing of the altarpiece from Snoza, painted in Poland about 1460. The martyr bishop of Prague stands in his mitre and vestments; the back of the panel shows the Virgin of the Annunciation. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.

agatha_of_sicily_virgin.label: The painting
agatha_of_sicily_virgin.text: Saint Agatha by Lorenzo Lippi, about 1638–44, a Florentine painter and poet. Calm and looking straight at us, she holds the shears of her martyrdom over the dish that became her emblem. It is in the Blanton Museum of Art, Austin, Texas.

agnes_of_rome_virgin.label: The painting
agnes_of_rome_virgin.text: Saint Agnes by Francesco Furini, the Florentine painter who became a parish priest, in the second quarter of the 1600s. She holds a lamb, her emblem, close against her shoulder: her name echoes agnus, the Latin for lamb.

albert_the_great_bishop.label: The painting
albert_the_great_bishop.text: The Sermon of Saint Albertus Magnus, a German panel by Friedrich Walther, about 1430. The great Dominican scholar preaches to a gathered crowd. It is in The Cloisters, the medieval branch of the Metropolitan Museum, New York.

all_saints.label: The painting
all_saints.text: The Adoration of the Trinity, known as the Landauer Altarpiece, by Albrecht Dürer, 1511. The whole Church of heaven and earth—popes, emperors, martyrs and ordinary people—gathers around the Trinity; Dürer painted himself in the corner. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

aloysius_gonzaga_religious.label: The painting
aloysius_gonzaga_religious.text: The Vocation of Saint Aloysius Gonzaga by Guercino, about 1650. The young nobleman lays aside his crown and turns to the crucifix, choosing religious life over his inheritance. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

alphonsus_mary_liguori_bishop.label: The portrait
alphonsus_mary_liguori_bishop.text: An engraved portrait of Alphonsus as an aged bishop, as printed in the Catholic Encyclopedia of 1907–13. Crippled by arthritis, he kept writing until his nineties; his books on prayer and on Mary were read for two centuries.

ambrose_of_milan_bishop.label: The altarpiece
ambrose_of_milan_bishop.text: A detail of the polyptych of Saint Ambrose by Giovanni Barbagelata, 1499, still in the parish church of Sant'Ambrogio in Varazze on the Ligurian coast. Ambrose is shown in bishop's robes, with the scourge he used against heresy.

andrew_apostle.label: The painting
andrew_apostle.text: The Martyrdom of Saint Andrew by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, painted in Seville around 1675–82. Andrew is bound to the X-shaped cross that became his emblem, as light breaks through the clouds above. It hangs in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.

andrew_dung_lac_priest_and_companions_ma.label: The painting
andrew_dung_lac_priest_and_companions_ma.text: A Vietnamese painting from the mid-1800s showing the execution of Paul Mi, Peter Duong and Peter Truat on December 18, 1838. Pictures like this were made at the time to record the martyrs, and some were carried back to Paris by missionaries.

angela_merici_virgin.label: The fresco
angela_merici_virgin.text: A fresco in the chapel of Saint Angela Merici at Tiarno di Sotto, in the mountains of Trentino. Angela is shown with her first companions, the young women of Brescia who became the Ursulines.

annunciation_of_the_lord.label: The painting
annunciation_of_the_lord.text: The Annunciation by Leonardo da Vinci, about 1472–76, painted when he was in his early twenties in Verrocchio's workshop in Florence. Gabriel kneels in a walled garden as Mary looks up from her book. It is in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.

anselm_of_canterbury_bishop.label: The fresco
anselm_of_canterbury_bishop.text: A ceiling painting by Josef Ferdinand Fromiller in the abbey church of Ossiach in Carinthia, Austria, from the 1740s. The Virgin Mary appears to Anselm in a burst of heavenly light.

ansgar_of_hamburg_bishop.label: The painting
ansgar_of_hamburg_bishop.text: Ansgar Preaching Christianity by Gustaf Cederström, 1889, a design for a mural in Sweden's Nationalmuseum. The monk preaches to the pagan Swedes at Birka, the first Christian mission in the country. It is in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.

anthony_of_egypt_abbot.label: The painting
anthony_of_egypt_abbot.text: Saint Anthony Abbot and Saint Paul the Hermit by Diego Velázquez, about 1634. A raven brings bread to the two old hermits; in the background Velázquez tells the rest of the story, including Anthony burying Paul with the help of two lions. It is in the Museo del Prado.

anthony_of_padua_priest.label: The painting
anthony_of_padua_priest.text: Saint Anthony of Padua with the Christ Child by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1668, painted for the Capuchin friary in Seville. It shows the most loved story about him: one night a visitor saw the infant Jesus appear in Anthony's arms. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Seville.

apollinaris_of_ravenna_bishop.label: The mosaic
apollinaris_of_ravenna_bishop.text: A detail of the 6th-century mosaic in the apse of Sant'Apollinare in Classe, near Ravenna. Apollinaris stands with arms raised in prayer among twelve lambs in a green paradise; the basilica was built over his grave.

ascension_of_the_lord.label: The painting
ascension_of_the_lord.text: The Ascension of Christ by Pietro Perugino, about 1495–98, painted for the Benedictine abbey of San Pietro in Perugia. The apostles and Mary look up as Christ rises in a ring of angels. It was taken by Napoleon's armies and is now in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Lyon.

assumption_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.label: The painting
assumption_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.text: The Assumption of the Virgin by Titian, 1516–18, the enormous altarpiece that made his name. Nearly seven meters high, it still stands above the high altar of the Frari church in Venice, where it was unveiled to the city's astonishment.

athanasius_of_alexandria_bishop.label: The icon
athanasius_of_alexandria_bishop.text: Saint Athanasius by Michael Damaskinos, a Cretan painter of the late 1500s who worked in both Byzantine and Venetian styles. It belongs to the Hellenic Institute of Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Studies in Venice.

augustine_of_canterbury_bishop.label: The illustration
augustine_of_canterbury_bishop.text: Augustine Preaching Before King Ethelbert, by James Doyle, from A Chronicle of England, 1864, printed in color by Edmund Evans. The king of Kent listens to the monks from Rome in the open air, wary of their magic indoors.

augustine_of_hippo_bishop.label: The painting
augustine_of_hippo_bishop.text: Saint Augustine by Philippe de Champaigne, about 1645–50. The flaming heart in his hand and the beam marked Veritas, truth, sum up his life's search. It is in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

augustine_zhao_rong_priest_and_companion.label: The icon
augustine_zhao_rong_priest_and_companion.text: An icon of the martyrs of the Boxer Rebellion of 1900, painted in 1990 at Holy Transfiguration Monastery in Brookline, Massachusetts. Eighty-six of the 120 Catholic martyrs of China canonized in 2000 died in that same uprising.

baptism_of_the_lord.label: The painting
baptism_of_the_lord.text: The Baptism of Christ by Andrea del Verrocchio and his pupil Leonardo da Vinci, about 1470–75. The young Leonardo painted the angel at far left; Vasari says Verrocchio was so outdone he gave up painting. It is in the Uffizi, Florence.

barnabas_apostle.label: The painting
barnabas_apostle.text: Paul and Barnabas at Lystra by Pieter Lastman, Rembrandt's teacher, 1617. After a healing, the crowd takes the apostles for the gods Zeus and Hermes and tries to sacrifice an ox to them; the apostles tear their clothes in protest. It is in the Amsterdam Museum.

bartholomew_apostle.label: The fresco
bartholomew_apostle.text: Saint Bartholomew, from Michelangelo's Last Judgment, 1536–41, on the altar wall of the Sistine Chapel. He holds the knife and his own flayed skin, and the face on the skin is thought to be Michelangelo's self-portrait.

basil_the_great_and_gregory_nazianzen_bi.label: The painting
basil_the_great_and_gregory_nazianzen_bi.text: Saint Basil by Peter Paul Rubens, an oil sketch from the early 1600s, showing the bishop in his vestments, deep in thought. It is in the Ducal Museum at Friedenstein Castle, Gotha, Germany.

bede_the_venerable_priest.label: The painting
bede_the_venerable_priest.text: The Last Chapter by James Doyle Penrose, an English painter of the early 1900s. It shows the story told by Bede's student Cuthbert: dying, Bede dictated the last words of his translation of St. John's Gospel, then sang 'Glory be' and died.

benedict_of_nursia_abbot.label: The fresco
benedict_of_nursia_abbot.text: Benedict Receives Maurus and Placidus, by Il Sodoma, 1505–08, from the great cycle of his life in the cloister of Monte Oliveto Maggiore, Tuscany. Two Roman noble families entrust their sons to him; both boys became saints.

bernard_of_clairvaux_abbot.label: The painting
bernard_of_clairvaux_abbot.text: The Vision of Saint Bernard by Filippino Lippi, about 1485. The Virgin appears to Bernard as he writes at a desk among the rocks, with angels at her side. It still hangs in the Badia Fiorentina, Florence.

bernardine_of_siena_priest.label: The painting
bernardine_of_siena_priest.text: Saint Bernardino of Siena Venerating the Crucifix, by Jacopo Bellini, about 1450–55, painted within a few years of the preacher's death. Jacopo was the father of Gentile and Giovanni Bellini. It is now in the United States.

blaise_of_sebaste_bishop.label: The painting
blaise_of_sebaste_bishop.text: The Martyrdom of Saint Blaise by Gaspar de Crayer, 1668, painted when the Flemish artist was in his eighties. The bishop is tortured with iron combs before his beheading. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Ghent.

bonaventure_of_bagnoregio_bishop.label: The painting
bonaventure_of_bagnoregio_bishop.text: The Lying-in-State of Saint Bonaventure by Francisco de Zurbarán, 1629. He died during the Council of Lyon, and the pope and the king of Aragon came to mourn him. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

boniface_of_mainz_bishop.label: The painting
boniface_of_mainz_bishop.text: Saint Boniface of Mainz by Albrecht De Vriendt, a Belgian history painter, 1889. Boniface, an Englishman, is remembered as the Apostle of Germany; he famously felled the sacred oak of Thor. It is in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts, Antwerp.

bridget_of_sweden_religious.label: The painting
bridget_of_sweden_religious.text: Saint Bridget of Sweden by the Florentine painter Maso da San Friano, from the mid-1500s. Bridget spent her last twenty-four years in Italy, where her Revelations were widely read. It is in the York Art Gallery, England.

bruno_of_cologne_priest.label: The painting
bruno_of_cologne_priest.text: Saint Bruno in Prayer by Domingos Sequeira, 1799–1800, painted for the Carthusian monastery of Laveiras near Lisbon. Sequeira was Portugal's leading painter of his day. It is in the National Museum of Ancient Art, Lisbon.

cajetan_of_thiene_priest.label: The painting
cajetan_of_thiene_priest.text: Saint Cajetan's Vision of the Holy Family by Giambattista Tiepolo, about 1735. On Christmas night in Rome, legend says, Mary placed the infant Jesus in Cajetan's arms. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.

camillus_de_lellis_priest.label: The painting
camillus_de_lellis_priest.text: Saint Camillus de Lellis Saving the Sick of the Santo Spirito Hospital from the Flood of 1598, by Pierre Subleyras, 1746. When the Tiber burst its banks, Camillus and his brothers carried the patients to safety on their backs. It is in the Museo di Roma, Palazzo Braschi.

casimir_of_poland.label: The watercolor
casimir_of_poland.text: Saint Casimir, Polish Crown Prince, a watercolor by Jan Matejko, 1863. The young prince kneels in prayer, his ermine-lined royal cloak slipping from his shoulders. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.

catherine_of_alexandria_virgin.label: The painting
catherine_of_alexandria_virgin.text: Saint Catherine of Alexandria by Caravaggio, about 1598, painted for his patron Cardinal del Monte. She kneels beside the broken spiked wheel, a sword in her hand. His model was a Roman courtesan, Fillide Melandroni. It is in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.

catherine_of_siena_virgin.label: The painting
catherine_of_siena_virgin.text: The Mystic Marriage of Saint Catherine of Siena by Fra Bartolomeo, 1511, painted for San Marco in Florence and given to the French ambassador. The Christ Child places a ring on her finger. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

cecilia_of_rome_virgin.label: The painting
cecilia_of_rome_virgin.text: The Ecstasy of Saint Cecilia by Raphael, about 1514–16. Cecilia lets her organ slip as she hears the music of angels; broken instruments lie at her feet. It is in the Pinacoteca Nazionale, Bologna.

chair_of_saint_peter_the_apostle.label: The painting
chair_of_saint_peter_the_apostle.text: Saint Peter Enthroned by Rodrigo de Osona, about 1475–85, one of the first painters in Valencia to work in the new Flemish manner. Peter sits on his throne as the first pope, wearing the papal tiara and holding the keys, with an angel on either side.

charles_borromeo_bishop.label: The painting
charles_borromeo_bishop.text: The Fast of Saint Charles Borromeo by Daniele Crespi, about 1628. The cardinal eats only bread and water as he reads, tears on his face. It is in the church of Santa Maria della Passione, Milan.

clare_of_assisi_virgin.label: The fresco
clare_of_assisi_virgin.text: Saint Clare by Simone Martini, about 1317–20, in the Lower Church of San Francesco, Assisi—the city where she lived and died. It is the classic image of her in the brown habit of her Poor Clares.

clement_i_pope.label: The painting
clement_i_pope.text: Saint Clement Striking the Rock by Bernardino Fungai, about 1500. Exiled to the Crimean mines, legend says, Clement saw a lamb on a hill and struck the rock there, and water gushed out for the thirsty prisoners. It is in the York Art Gallery.

columban_of_luxeuil_abbot.label: The fresco
columban_of_luxeuil_abbot.text: A fresco in the hermitage of San Colombano at Trambileno, Trentino, a tiny chapel built into a cliff face above a gorge. It is one of many places across Europe named for the wandering Irish monk.

commemoration_of_all_the_faithful_depart.label: The painting
commemoration_of_all_the_faithful_depart.text: The Day of the Dead by William-Adolphe Bouguereau, 1859. Two women in mourning pray at a grave, the younger leaning on the older in her grief. It is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Bordeaux.

conversion_of_saint_paul_the_apostle.label: The painting
conversion_of_saint_paul_the_apostle.text: The Conversion on the Way to Damascus by Caravaggio, 1601. Saul lies on his back beneath his horse, arms flung open to a light only he can see. It still hangs where it was made for, in the Cerasi Chapel of Santa Maria del Popolo, Rome.

cosmas_of_cilicia_and_damian_of_cilicia_.label: The painting
cosmas_of_cilicia_and_damian_of_cilicia_.text: The Healing of Deacon Justinian by Fra Angelico, about 1438–40, from the San Marco altarpiece in Florence. The twin doctors replace a deacon's diseased leg with that of a dead man. It is in the Museum of San Marco, Florence.

cyril_constantine_the_philosopher_monk_a.label: The painting
cyril_constantine_the_philosopher_monk_a.text: An altar painting of Saints Cyril and Methodius in the church dedicated to them in Karlín, Prague, built in the 1850s–60s. The brothers hold the Slavonic Scriptures they translated.

cyril_of_alexandria_bishop.label: The fresco
cyril_of_alexandria_bishop.text: A detail of the frescoes of the Chora Church in Istanbul, about 1320, among the finest late Byzantine paintings. Cyril appears among the great bishops of the Church in the side chapel.

cyril_of_jerusalem_bishop.label: The painting
cyril_of_jerusalem_bishop.text: A painting by Palma il Giovane, about 1590, in the sacristy of the Chiesa dei Gesuiti in Venice. Cyril of Jerusalem appears in a cycle on the legendary history of the Crutched Friars.

damasus_i_pope.label: The altarpiece
damasus_i_pope.text: Saint Jerome in Penitence with Saints and Donors by Francesco Botticini, about 1490. Pope Damasus, who asked Jerome to revise the Latin Bible, stands in his red robes on the left beside Saint Eusebius; Saints Paula and Eustochium stand on the right. It is in the National Gallery, London.

dedication_of_the_basilica_of_saint_mary.label: The painting
dedication_of_the_basilica_of_saint_mary.text: The Founding of Santa Maria Maggiore by Masolino, about 1428. Christ and Mary send snow on an August night, and Pope Liberius traces the church's outline in it. It was the center of an altarpiece painted with Masaccio and is in the Capodimonte Museum, Naples.

dedication_of_the_basilicas_of_saints_pe.label: The painting
dedication_of_the_basilicas_of_saints_pe.text: St. Peter's, Rome, by Viviano Codazzi, about 1630. Michelangelo's dome had been finished only a few decades earlier. It is in the Museo del Prado.

dedication_of_the_lateran_basilica.label: The painting
dedication_of_the_lateran_basilica.text: The Basilica of Saint John Lateran by Giacomo van Lint, a painter of views of Rome, in the later 1700s. Alessandro Galilei's great façade rises over the open square, with the Lateran Palace, the old home of the popes, beside it.

denis_of_paris_bishop_and_companions_mar.label: The altarpiece
denis_of_paris_bishop_and_companions_mar.text: The Altarpiece of Saint Denis by Henri Bellechose, 1416, painted for the Charterhouse of Champmol in Dijon. Christ gives Denis his last communion in prison, and beside it he and his companions are beheaded. It is in the Louvre.

dominic_de_guzman_priest.label: The painting
dominic_de_guzman_priest.text: The Feast of the Rose Garlands by Albrecht Dürer, 1506, painted in Venice for German merchants. Mary and the Christ Child crown the pope and emperor with roses, while Dominic, at left, crowns the faithful. It is in the National Gallery Prague.

easter_sunday.label: The painting
easter_sunday.text: The Resurrection, a panel from a Netherlandish altarpiece of about 1485–1500. Christ steps from the tomb with the banner of victory as the soldiers sleep or wake in fright; behind them the story goes on, from Christ freeing the souls of the dead to the women on their way to the tomb and the Ascension. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

easter_monday.label: The painting
easter_monday.text: The Three Marys at the Tomb, about 1425–35, by Jan van Eyck and perhaps his brother Hubert. An angel sits on the open tomb while the soldiers sleep, with an imagined Jerusalem behind. It is in the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam.

easter_tuesday.label: The fresco
easter_tuesday.text: Noli me tangere by Fra Angelico, about 1440–42, painted on the wall of a friar's cell at the Convent of San Marco in Florence. Christ carries a hoe, as the gardener Mary takes him for, in a meadow scattered with flowers.

easter_wednesday.label: The painting
easter_wednesday.text: The Supper at Emmaus by Caravaggio, 1601. The moment Christ blesses the bread, one disciple grips his chair and the other flings out his arms. It is in the National Gallery, London.

easter_thursday.label: The painting
easter_thursday.text: Christ Appears Behind Locked Doors by Duccio, 1308–11, a panel from his great Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral. It is in the Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Siena.

easter_friday.label: The painting
easter_friday.text: The Miraculous Draught of Fishes by Konrad Witz, 1444, from an altarpiece for Geneva Cathedral. It is often called the first realistic landscape in European art: the lake and mountains are the real view across Lake Geneva. It is in the Musée d'Art et d'Histoire, Geneva.

easter_saturday.label: The painting
easter_saturday.text: Christ and St Mary Magdalen at the Tomb by Rembrandt, 1638. Christ wears a gardener's hat and holds a spade, and dawn breaks over Jerusalem. It is in the Royal Collection, Buckingham Palace, London.

elizabeth_ann_seton_religious.label: The portrait
elizabeth_ann_seton_religious.text: Elizabeth Ann Bayley Seton by Charles Balthazar Julien Févret de Saint-Mémin, 1797, when she was a young New York wife and mother. The French émigré made precise profile portraits using a tracing machine called a physiognotrace. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

elizabeth_of_hungary_religious.label: The fresco
elizabeth_of_hungary_religious.text: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary by Simone Martini, about 1317–20, among the saints he painted in the Lower Church of San Francesco, Assisi. She died less than a century before, and the Franciscans already counted her as one of their own.

elizabeth_of_portugal.label: The painting
elizabeth_of_portugal.text: Saint Elizabeth of Portugal by Francisco de Zurbarán, about 1635. She carries roses in her skirt: legend says the bread she was secretly taking to the poor turned to roses when her husband stopped her. It is in the Museo del Prado.

ephrem_the_syrian_deacon.label: The icon
ephrem_the_syrian_deacon.text: The Death of Ephrem the Syrian, a Cretan icon by Emmanuel Tzanfournaris, 17th century. Monks and hermits from across the desert gather around the body of the poet-saint. It is in the Vatican Pinacoteca.

epiphany_of_the_lord.label: The painting
epiphany_of_the_lord.text: The Adoration of the Kings by Hugo van der Goes, about 1470, called the Monforte Altarpiece after the Spanish monastery of Monforte de Lemos, where it stayed until 1914. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

eusebius_of_vercelli_bishop.label: The painting
eusebius_of_vercelli_bishop.text: The Virgin in Glory with the Archangel Gabriel and Saints Eusebius, Sebastian and Roch, by Sebastiano Ricci, 1724–25, one of the last works of the Venetian painter. It belongs to the University of Turin.

exaltation_of_the_holy_cross.label: The painting
exaltation_of_the_holy_cross.text: Heraclius Carrying the Cross, from the Frankfurt altarpiece of the Exaltation of the True Cross by Adam Elsheimer, about 1603–05. Painted on copper, it is barely larger than a book. The emperor brings the Cross back to Jerusalem barefoot, having laid aside his crown. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.

fabian_i_pope.label: The painting
fabian_i_pope.text: The Madonna Enthroned with Saints by Paris Bordone, about 1530, a Venetian pupil of Titian. Pope Fabian, martyred in 250, joins the saints around the throne. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

fidelis_of_sigmaringen_priest.label: The painting
fidelis_of_sigmaringen_priest.text: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen and Saint Joseph of Leonessa by Giambattista Tiepolo, 1752–58. Both were Capuchin friars and missionaries; Fidelis was killed preaching in Switzerland. It is in the Galleria Nazionale, Parma.

first_martyrs_of_the_holy_roman_church.label: The painting
first_martyrs_of_the_holy_roman_church.text: Nero's Torches by Henryk Siemiradzki, 1876, a canvas seven meters wide. Christians are bound to stakes, about to be set alight, as the emperor arrives for the spectacle. It is in the Sukiennice gallery of the National Museum in Kraków.

frances_of_rome_religious.label: The painting
frances_of_rome_religious.text: Head of Saint Francesca Romana by Orazio Gentileschi, about 1618. Gentileschi was the father of the painter Artemisia. It is on deposit at the Petit Palais, Paris.

francis_de_sales_bishop.label: The painting
francis_de_sales_bishop.text: Saint Francis de Sales, Bishop of Geneva, an early 17th-century portrait at the Château de Bussy-Rabutin in Burgundy. The house belonged to the Rabutin family, into which Francis's friend St. Jane de Chantal had married.

francis_of_assisi.label: The painting
francis_of_assisi.text: Saint Francis in the Desert by Giovanni Bellini, about 1480. Francis steps out of his cave into a flood of light, arms open, perhaps at the moment of the stigmata. It is often called the greatest Italian Renaissance painting in America. It is in the Frick Collection, New York.

francis_of_paola_hermit.label: The painting
francis_of_paola_hermit.text: The Madonna and Child with Saint Francis of Paola by Francesco Solimena, about 1704. The old hermit kneels on a cloud, his staff beside him. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

francis_xavier_priest.label: The painting
francis_xavier_priest.text: The famous Japanese portrait of Francis Xavier, painted in the early 1600s and found in 1920, hidden in the home of a family of secret Christians near Osaka. He gazes up at the cross, his heart aflame. It is in the Kobe City Museum.

george_of_lydda_martyr.label: The painting
george_of_lydda_martyr.text: Saint George and the Dragon by Raphael, about 1506. George wears the Order of the Garter below his knee, perhaps because the picture was a gift for King Henry VII of England. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

gertrude_the_great_virgin.label: The painting
gertrude_the_great_virgin.text: Saint Gertrude by Miguel Cabrera, 1763, the leading painter of colonial Mexico. Gertrude was hugely popular in New Spain; the Christ Child appears in her heart. It is in the Dallas Museum of Art.

gregory_i_the_great_pope.label: The painting
gregory_i_the_great_pope.text: Saint Gregory the Great by Francisco de Goya, 1796–99, one of his four Doctors of the Church. The pope writes at his desk in his tiara and robes. It is in the Museo del Romanticismo, Madrid.

gregory_of_narek_abbot.label: The illumination
gregory_of_narek_abbot.text: The oldest portrait of Gregory of Narek, from a manuscript of his Book of Lamentations copied in 1173, less than two centuries after his death. It is in the Matenadaran, the great library of ancient manuscripts in Yerevan, Armenia.

gregory_vii_pope.label: The painting
gregory_vii_pope.text: Pope Gregory VII Protecting the Envoy Orlando of Parma by Francesco Hayez, 1857. Henry IV's messenger brought a letter deposing the pope, and the Roman synod nearly killed him; Gregory shielded him. Hayez was the leading painter of Romantic Italy.

hedwig_of_silesia_religious.label: The illumination
hedwig_of_silesia_religious.text: Saint Hedwig with Duke Ludwig of Legnica and Duchess Agnes, from the Hedwig Codex, 1353. She holds a statue of the Virgin, a rosary and the shoes she carried rather than wore, to walk barefoot. It is in the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles.

henry_ii_emperor.label: The painting
henry_ii_emperor.text: The Heinrichstafel, a panel by the Master of the Legend of Saint Barbara, Brussels, about 1490. It tells the story of the emperor: his coronation in Rome, a vision of the Cross and his victory in battle.

hilary_of_poitiers_bishop.label: The embroidery
hilary_of_poitiers_bishop.text: Saint Martin and Saint Hilary, a Flemish embroidered roundel of about 1430–35, once sewn onto a priest's vestment. Hilary was the bishop who first welcomed the young soldier Martin to Poitiers. It is in the Robert Lehman Collection of the Metropolitan Museum, New York.

hildegard_of_bingen_abbess.label: The illumination
hildegard_of_bingen_abbess.text: Hildegard receiving a vision, from the Rupertsberg manuscript of her Scivias, made under her supervision around 1180. Flames of light descend on her head as she writes on a wax tablet and the monk Volmar takes it down. The original was lost in 1945; a hand-painted copy survives.

holy_family_of_jesus_mary_and_joseph.label: The painting
holy_family_of_jesus_mary_and_joseph.text: The Doni Tondo by Michelangelo, about 1506, his only finished panel painting. It was made for the wedding of Agnolo Doni in Florence. The Child passes between Mary and Joseph, with nude youths behind and the infant John the Baptist. It is in the Uffizi, still in its original carved frame.

holy_guardian_angels.label: The painting
holy_guardian_angels.text: The Guardian Angel by Domenichino, 1615. The angel shields a child with one hand and drives off the devil with the other. It is in the Capodimonte Museum, Naples.

holy_innocents_martyrs.label: The painting
holy_innocents_martyrs.text: The Massacre of the Innocents by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1638, one of two he painted of the subject. Mothers fight Herod's soldiers for their children as cherubs bring the martyrs' crowns from above. It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.

ignatius_of_antioch_bishop.label: The painting
ignatius_of_antioch_bishop.text: Saint Ignatius of Antioch, an Italian panel of about 1486. He holds a heart: legend says that after his death the name of Jesus was found written on his heart. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ignatius_of_loyola_priest.label: The painting
ignatius_of_loyola_priest.text: The Miracles of Saint Ignatius of Loyola by Peter Paul Rubens, 1617–18, painted for the high altar of the new Jesuit church in Antwerp. Ignatius drives out demons and heals the sick. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

immaculate_conception_of_the_blessed_vir.label: The painting
immaculate_conception_of_the_blessed_vir.text: The Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1678. Looted from Seville by Napoleon's Marshal Soult, it was bought by the Louvre in 1852 for the highest price ever paid for a painting, and returned to Spain in 1941. It is in the Museo del Prado.

immaculate_heart_of_mary.label: The painting
immaculate_heart_of_mary.text: The Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary by Vicente López Portaña, about 1830, court painter to the Spanish kings. It is in the Diocesan Museum of Sacred Art in Orihuela, Spain.

independence_day.label: The painting
independence_day.text: Declaration of Independence by John Trumbull, commissioned by Congress in 1817. It shows the drafting committee—Adams, Sherman, Livingston, Jefferson and Franklin—presenting their work in Philadelphia. It hangs in the Rotunda of the U.S. Capitol and is on the back of the two-dollar bill.

irenaeus_of_lyon_bishop.label: The icon
irenaeus_of_lyon_bishop.text: A modern icon of Irenaeus of Lyon. As a boy in Asia Minor he heard St. Polycarp, who had known St. John the Apostle—a living link between the apostles and the Church in Gaul.

isidore_of_seville_bishop.label: The painting
isidore_of_seville_bishop.text: Saint Isidore of Seville by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, 1655, painted for the sacristy of Seville Cathedral, where Isidore had been archbishop. He is shown as a scholar, absorbed in a book. It is still in the cathedral.

isidore_the_farmer.label: The painting
isidore_the_farmer.text: Saint Isidore: the Blessing of Work, by Marcello Bacciarelli, 1805, court painter to the last King of Poland. Legend says angels drove the plow while Isidore prayed. It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.

james_apostle.label: The painting
james_apostle.text: Saint James the Apostle by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1612–13, from his apostle series for the Duke of Lerma. He carries the pilgrim's staff of Santiago de Compostela. The series is in the Prado.

jane_frances_de_chantal_religious.label: The painting
jane_frances_de_chantal_religious.text: Saint Francis de Sales Giving Saint Jane de Chantal the Rule of the Visitation, by Noël Hallé, 18th century. It hangs in the church of Saint-Louis-en-l'Île, Paris.

januarius_i_of_benevento_bishop.label: The painting
januarius_i_of_benevento_bishop.text: Saint Januarius Emerges Unharmed from the Furnace by Jusepe de Ribera, 1646, painted on copper. It is in the Chapel of the Treasure of San Gennaro in Naples Cathedral, where the vial of his blood is kept.

jerome_emiliani.label: The painting
jerome_emiliani.text: Saint Jerome Emiliani by Giandomenico Tiepolo, 1759, from the private chapel of the Tiepolo family villa at Zianigo. It is now in Ca' Rezzonico, Venice.

jerome_of_stridon_priest.label: The painting
jerome_of_stridon_priest.text: Saint Jerome Writing by Caravaggio, 1607–08, painted in Malta for the knight Ippolito Malaspina, whose coat of arms is in the corner. Stolen in 1984 and recovered in 1988, it hangs in St. John's Co-Cathedral, Valletta.

joachim_and_anne_parents_of_mary.label: The painting
joachim_and_anne_parents_of_mary.text: The Meeting of Joachim and Anne at the Golden Gate by Filippino Lippi, 1497. Told separately by angels that they would have a child, the elderly couple embrace at the gate of Jerusalem. It is in the National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen.

john_apostle.label: The painting
john_apostle.text: Saint John on Patmos by Hieronymus Bosch, about 1489. John gazes at a vision of the Woman clothed with the sun while a little devil tries to steal his ink. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

john_baptist_de_la_salle_priest.label: The engraving
john_baptist_de_la_salle_priest.text: Jean-Baptiste de La Salle, engraved by L. Chapon after Charles Müller for an 1887 Life of the saint. He is shown as a teacher among his pupils, the poor boys of Reims for whom he founded his schools.

john_chrysostom_bishop.label: The mosaic
john_chrysostom_bishop.text: Saint John Chrysostom, a mosaic of the late 800s in the north tympanum of Hagia Sophia, Istanbul, where he was archbishop. His name, 'golden-mouthed', is spelled out in gold beside him.

john_damascene_priest.label: The fresco
john_damascene_priest.text: Saint John of Damascus in a 14th or 15th-century fresco on Mount Athos. He wears the turban he would have worn as an official at the Caliph's court in Damascus, before he became a monk.

john_de_brebeuf_isaac_jogues_priests_and.label: The portrait
john_de_brebeuf_isaac_jogues_priests_and.text: Isaac Jogues, from a portrait published in 1904, holding a page with the Jesuit motto Ad majorem Dei gloriam. Captured and tortured by the Mohawks in 1642, he escaped, went back, and was killed at Ossernenon, in today's New York, in 1646. It is in the Library of Congress.

john_fisher_bishop_and_thomas_more_marty.label: The painting
john_fisher_bishop_and_thomas_more_marty.text: Sir Thomas More by Hans Holbein the Younger, 1527, painted while Holbein lived in More's household in Chelsea. More wears the gold chain of royal service he would later lose with his life. It is in the Frick Collection, New York.

john_henry_newman_priest.label: The painting
john_henry_newman_priest.text: Cardinal Newman by Sir John Everett Millais, 1881, painted two years after Newman was made a cardinal at seventy-eight. It belongs to the National Portrait Gallery, London.

john_i_pope.label: The print
john_i_pope.text: Pope John I, a chromolithograph from 1879, one of a series of portraits of all the popes from St. Peter to Leo XIII. No real likeness of him survives.

john_leonardi_priest.label: The painting
john_leonardi_priest.text: Saint John Leonardi with the Virgin and Child, an altar painting showing the founder among the young people he taught. A pharmacist's assistant turned priest, he helped found the Vatican's college for training missionaries.

john_mary_vianney_priest.label: The portrait
john_mary_vianney_priest.text: 'Authentic portrait of the holy Curé of Ars, made from life', a 19th-century French print of the priest of Ars in his last days. It is in the National Library of France.

john_of_avila_priest.label: The painting
john_of_avila_priest.text: Portrait of Juan de Ávila from the workshop of El Greco, about 1580. It is in the El Greco Museum, Toledo.

john_of_capistrano_priest.label: The altarpiece
john_of_capistrano_priest.text: The Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints by Carlo Crivelli, 1488, painted for a Franciscan church in the Marche. John of Capistrano, canonized centuries later, already appears among the Franciscan saints around the throne. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

john_of_god_duarte_cidade_religious.label: The painting
john_of_god_duarte_cidade_religious.text: Saint John of God Carrying a Sick Man by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1672. Exhausted, he stumbles under his burden, and an angel steps in to help him. It hangs in the Hospital de la Caridad, Seville.

john_of_kanty_priest.label: The painting
john_of_kanty_priest.text: A Miracle of Saint John of Kanty by Taddeo Kuntze, about 1767. The Kraków professor was known for giving away his own clothes and food to the poor. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.

john_of_the_cross_priest.label: The painting
john_of_the_cross_priest.text: Christ Crucified with a Carmelite friar, probably John of the Cross, attributed to Agustín del Castillo, early 1600s. John's own small drawing of Christ on the cross, seen from above, later inspired Salvador Dalí. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts of Córdoba.

josaphat_kuntsevych_bishop.label: The painting
josaphat_kuntsevych_bishop.text: The Martyrdom of Saint Josaphat Kuntsevych by Józef Simmler, about 1861. The archbishop was killed by a mob at Vitebsk in 1623. It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.

joseph_of_calasanz_priest.label: The painting
joseph_of_calasanz_priest.text: The Last Communion of Saint Joseph Calasanz by Francisco de Goya, 1819, painted for the Piarist church of San Antón in Madrid. Goya had studied at a Piarist school as a boy and refused most of his fee. It is still in San Antón.

joseph_spouse_of_mary.label: The painting
joseph_spouse_of_mary.text: The Marriage of the Virgin by Raphael, 1504, painted at twenty-one and proudly signed on the temple. Joseph holds the rod that miraculously blossomed to show he was God's choice; a rejected suitor breaks his over his knee. It is in the Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan.

joseph_the_worker.label: The painting
joseph_the_worker.text: Saint Joseph the Carpenter by Georges de La Tour, about 1642. The boy Jesus holds a candle for Joseph as he bores into a beam that foreshadows the cross. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

juan_diego_cuauhtlatoatzin.label: The painting
juan_diego_cuauhtlatoatzin.text: Saint Juan Diego with the Tilma, a Mexican painting of 1737. He opens his cloak to show the roses he gathered in December, and the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe on the cloth.

lawrence_of_brindisi_priest.label: The engraving
lawrence_of_brindisi_priest.text: Lawrence of Brindisi, an engraving by Franz Heissig, about 1770–80. The Capuchin preacher, with his long white beard, holds a crucifix. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

lawrence_of_rome_deacon.label: The painting
lawrence_of_rome_deacon.text: The Martyrdom of Saint Lawrence by Titian, 1548–59, one of the first great night pictures in Western art, lit by torches and the fire beneath the gridiron. It is in the Chiesa dei Gesuiti, Venice.

leo_i_the_great_pope.label: The fresco
leo_i_the_great_pope.text: The Meeting of Leo the Great and Attila by Raphael and his workshop, 1514, in the Vatican's Stanza di Eliodoro. Peter and Paul appear in the sky with swords as Attila turns back from Rome. Leo has the face of Raphael's patron, Pope Leo X.

louis_ix_of_france.label: The painting
louis_ix_of_france.text: Saint Louis, King of France, with a Page, by El Greco, about 1592–95. The crusader king holds his scepter while a page carries his crown. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

lucy_of_syracuse_virgin.label: The painting
lucy_of_syracuse_virgin.text: The Burial of Saint Lucy by Caravaggio, 1608, painted in Syracuse while he was on the run. Two huge gravediggers dwarf the mourners around her body. It was painted for the church of Santa Lucia al Sepolcro, built over the place of her burial.

luke_evangelist.label: The painting
luke_evangelist.text: Saint Luke Drawing the Virgin by Rogier van der Weyden, about 1435–40, perhaps with Rogier's own face as Luke. It was probably made for the painters' guild of Brussels, whose patron Luke was. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

margaret_mary_alacoque_virgin.label: The painting
margaret_mary_alacoque_virgin.text: The Vision of the Sacred Heart, a 19th-century canvas in the sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Acero in the Apennines. In the convent chapel at Paray-le-Monial, Christ shows Margaret Mary his heart, 'which has so loved mankind.'

margaret_of_scotland.label: The painting
margaret_of_scotland.text: Queen Saint Margaret of Scotland by Nicolas de Largillière, 1692, one of the leading portrait painters of Louis XIV's France. It hangs at Sizergh Castle in Cumbria, a National Trust house.

mark_evangelist.label: The painting
mark_evangelist.text: Saint Mark Preaching in Alexandria by Gentile and Giovanni Bellini, 1504–07, painted for the confraternity of St. Mark in Venice. Gentile died before it was finished and his brother completed it. Alexandria's great church looks remarkably like St. Mark's in Venice. It is in the Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan.

martha_of_bethany_mary_of_bethany_and_la.label: The painting
martha_of_bethany_mary_of_bethany_and_la.text: Christ in the House of Martha and Mary by Johannes Vermeer, about 1654–55, his largest painting and one of his very few religious scenes. Martha sets down the bread as Mary listens at Jesus's feet. It is in the Scottish National Gallery, Edinburgh.

martin_i_pope.label: The illustration
martin_i_pope.text: Pope Martin I Taken Prisoner, an engraving of about 1868 from a German history of the popes. In 653 the emperor's soldiers seized Martin in the Lateran and carried him off to Constantinople for trial.

martin_of_tours_bishop.label: The painting
martin_of_tours_bishop.text: Saint Martin and the Beggar by El Greco, 1597–99, painted for the Chapel of San José in Toledo. Martin, in gold-damascened armor on a white horse, slices his cloak for the beggar. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

mary_magdalene.label: The painting
mary_magdalene.text: The Penitent Magdalene by Titian, about 1533, painted for the Duke of Urbino. She looks to heaven, wrapped only in her golden hair. Titian painted the subject many times, but this is the most celebrated. It is in the Palazzo Pitti, Florence.

mary_magdalene_de_pazzi_virgin.label: The painting
mary_magdalene_de_pazzi_virgin.text: Saint Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi Crowned with Thorns by Marcos da Cruz, about 1675. The Florentine Carmelite mystic receives Christ's crown in a vision. It is in the National Museum of Ancient Art, Lisbon.

mary_mother_of_god.label: The icon
mary_mother_of_god.text: The Virgin of Vladimir, painted in Constantinople in the early 1100s and sent as a gift to Kiev. The Child presses his cheek to his mother's—the tender image called Eleousa, 'merciful'. It was credited with saving Moscow from Tamerlane, and is in the Tretyakov Gallery's church of St. Nicholas.

mary_mother_of_the_church.label: The painting
mary_mother_of_the_church.text: Pentecost by Juan Bautista Maíno, 1615–20, painted for a convent in Toledo. Mary sits at the center of the apostles as the Spirit descends—the Church gathered around her. It is in the Museo del Prado.

matthew_apostle.label: The painting
matthew_apostle.text: The Calling of Saint Matthew by Caravaggio, 1599–1600, his first great public commission. A beam of light follows Christ's pointing hand across a tavern table to the tax collector. It still hangs in the Contarelli Chapel of San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome.

matthias_apostle.label: The painting
matthias_apostle.text: Saint Matthias by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1611, from his series of the apostles. He holds the axe of his martyrdom. The series is in the Prado, Madrid.

michael_gabriel_and_raphael_archangels.label: The painting
michael_gabriel_and_raphael_archangels.text: The Fall of the Rebel Angels by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1562. Michael, in gleaming armor, drives the fallen angels from heaven as they turn into fantastic monsters. It is in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts, Brussels.

monica_of_hippo.label: The painting
monica_of_hippo.text: Saint Augustine and Saint Monica by Ary Scheffer, painted in the 1850s. Mother and son sit at a window at Ostia, gazing upward, as in Augustine's account of their shared vision of heaven days before her death. This version is in the Musée de la Vie Romantique, Scheffer's own house in Paris.

most_holy_body_and_blood_of_christ.label: The fresco
most_holy_body_and_blood_of_christ.text: The Disputation of the Holy Sacrament by Raphael, 1509–10, in the Vatican's Stanza della Segnatura. Heaven and earth meet at the monstrance on the altar: the Trinity and saints above, popes, theologians and Dante below.

most_holy_name_of_jesus.label: The painting
most_holy_name_of_jesus.text: The Adoration of the Shepherds by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1650. Rough Andalusian shepherds bring a lamb and eggs to the Child in Mary's lap. It is in the Museo del Prado.

most_holy_name_of_mary.label: The painting
most_holy_name_of_mary.text: The Madonna and Child with Angels by Giovanni Battista Salvi, called Sassoferrato, 17th century, famous for his serene Madonnas in pure ultramarine blue. It is in the Galleria Nazionale di Palazzo Corsini, Rome.

most_holy_trinity.label: The icon
most_holy_trinity.text: The Trinity by Andrei Rublev, about 1411–25, the most celebrated of all Russian icons. The three angels who visited Abraham sit around a table, a figure of Father, Son and Spirit in silent communion. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

most_sacred_heart_of_jesus.label: The painting
most_sacred_heart_of_jesus.text: The Sacred Heart of Jesus by Pompeo Batoni, 1767, painted for the Church of the Gesù in Rome, where it hangs. It became the model for countless devotional images of the Sacred Heart around the world.

nativity_of_john_the_baptist.label: The fresco
nativity_of_john_the_baptist.text: The Birth of Saint John the Baptist by Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1486–90, in the Tornabuoni Chapel of Santa Maria Novella, Florence. Elegant Florentine ladies visit Elizabeth, as if the birth had taken place in their own city.

nativity_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.label: The painting
nativity_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.text: The Birth of the Virgin by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1660, painted for Seville Cathedral. The newborn Mary glows in the arms of the midwives as angels crowd in to see her. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

nativity_of_the_lord.label: The painting
nativity_of_the_lord.text: The Adoration of the Child by Gerard van Honthorst, about 1620. All the light comes from the baby. Badly damaged by a car bomb outside the Uffizi in 1993, it was restored and hangs again in the Uffizi, Florence.

nereus_of_terracina_and_achilleus_of_ter.label: The painting
nereus_of_terracina_and_achilleus_of_ter.text: Saints Domitilla, Nereus and Achilleus by Peter Paul Rubens, 1608, painted on slate for the high altar of the Chiesa Nuova in Rome, where it still hangs. Nereus and Achilleus were soldiers who became Christians and were martyred.

nicholas_of_myra_bishop.label: The painting
nicholas_of_myra_bishop.text: Saint Nicholas Saves Three Innocents from Death by Ilya Repin, 1888. The bishop seizes the executioner's sword just before it falls. It is in the State Russian Museum, St. Petersburg.

norbert_of_xanten_bishop.label: The painting
norbert_of_xanten_bishop.text: The Citizens of Antwerp Return the Sacred Vessels to Saint Norbert by Cornelis de Vos, 1630. The people of Antwerp had hidden them during the heresy of Tanchelm. It is in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts, Antwerp.

our_lady_of_guadalupe.label: The image
our_lady_of_guadalupe.text: The original image of Our Lady of Guadalupe on Juan Diego's cloak, from 1531. It hangs above the altar of the Basilica of Guadalupe in Mexico City, the most visited Marian shrine in the world, where visitors pass beneath it on a moving walkway.

our_lady_of_loreto.label: The painting
our_lady_of_loreto.text: The Madonna di Loreto by Caravaggio, about 1604–06. Mary, barefoot in a Roman doorway, shows the Child to two kneeling pilgrims whose dirty feet scandalized some who saw it. It hangs in the church of Sant'Agostino, Rome.

our_lady_of_lourdes.label: The painting
our_lady_of_lourdes.text: Our Lady of Lourdes by Virgilio Tojetti, 1877. Bernadette kneels before the Lady in the grotto of Massabielle, where eighteen apparitions took place in 1858.

our_lady_of_mount_carmel.label: The painting
our_lady_of_mount_carmel.text: Our Lady of Mount Carmel by Onorio Marinari, 17th century, in the church of San Bartolomeo in Cutigliano, Tuscany. The Virgin and Child appear to Carmelite saints.

our_lady_of_sorrows.label: The painting
our_lady_of_sorrows.text: Mater Dolorosa with Clasped Hands by Titian, 1554, painted for the Emperor Charles V, who kept it with him when he retired to the monastery of Yuste. It is in the Museo del Prado.

our_lady_of_the_rosary.label: The painting
our_lady_of_the_rosary.text: The Madonna of the Rosary by Caravaggio, about 1605–07. Dominic hands out rosaries to the poor. Rubens and other Antwerp artists bought it for the Dominican church there; it is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

our_lord_jesus_christ_king_of_the_univer.label: The icon
our_lord_jesus_christ_king_of_the_univer.text: Christ Pantocrator, 'ruler of all', by Angelos Akotantos, the leading Cretan icon painter of the early 1400s. Christ blesses with one hand and holds the Gospel in the other.

pancras_of_rome_martyr.label: The altarpiece
pancras_of_rome_martyr.text: The San Pancrazio Polyptych by Bernardo Daddi, about 1336–40, painted for the church of San Pancrazio in Florence. The boy martyr Pancras, only fourteen, stands among the saints beside the Virgin. It is in the Uffizi, Florence.

passion_of_saint_john_the_baptist.label: The painting
passion_of_saint_john_the_baptist.text: The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist by Caravaggio, 1608, his largest painting and the only one he signed—in the blood flowing from John's neck. It hangs in the Oratory of St. John's Co-Cathedral, Valletta, Malta.

patrick_of_ireland_bishop.label: The painting
patrick_of_ireland_bishop.text: Saint Patrick, Bishop of Ireland, by Giambattista Tiepolo, 1746, painted for a church in Padua. Patrick raises his hand in blessing over a sick man at his feet. It is in the Musei Civici, Padua.

paul_miki_and_companions_martyrs.label: The painting
paul_miki_and_companions_martyrs.text: The Martyrs of Nagasaki, a painting from Prague. The twenty-six martyrs of 1597 are raised on crosses on a hill above Nagasaki and pierced with lances.

paulinus_of_nola_bishop.label: The painting
paulinus_of_nola_bishop.text: Saint Paulinus of Nola, an 18th-century canvas in the Diocesan Museum of Caltagirone, Sicily. Paulinus, a rich Roman senator and poet, gave away his fortune to become a priest and bishop of Nola.

pentecost_sunday.label: The painting
pentecost_sunday.text: Pentecost by El Greco, about 1600, one of his last great altarpieces. Flames burn above the apostles' heads around Mary at the center; the bald man looking out at upper right may be El Greco himself. It is in the Museo del Prado.

perpetua_of_carthage_and_felicity_of_car.label: The painting
perpetua_of_carthage_and_felicity_of_car.text: The Virgin and Child with Saints Felicity and Perpetua, an Italian panel of about 1520. The noblewoman and her slave died together in the arena at Carthage in 203. It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.

peter_and_paul_apostles.label: The painting
peter_and_paul_apostles.text: Saint Peter and Saint Paul by El Greco, 1587–92. Gentle, downcast Peter with his keys and fiery Paul with his book—two temperaments, one faith. It is in the Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.

peter_canisius_priest.label: The portrait
peter_canisius_priest.text: Saint Peter Canisius, an anonymous portrait. The Dutch Jesuit's catechisms went through hundreds of editions in his lifetime and he was called the second apostle of Germany.

peter_chrysologus_bishop.label: The engraving
peter_chrysologus_bishop.text: Saint Peter Chrysologus, from Jacques Callot's Images of All the Saints, 1636, a small engraving for every day of the year. The bishop of Ravenna, whose sermons earned him the name 'golden word', stands in a quiet landscape. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

philip_and_james_apostles.label: The painting
philip_and_james_apostles.text: The Martyrdom of Saint Philip by Jusepe de Ribera, 1639. Men strain to hoist the apostle onto his cross as the crowd watches. For two centuries it was thought to show St. Bartholomew. It is in the Museo del Prado.

philip_neri_priest.label: The painting
philip_neri_priest.text: Saint Philip Neri by Carlo Dolci, 1645–46. The joyful founder of the Oratory was known as the Apostle of Rome. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

pius_v_pope.label: The painting
pius_v_pope.text: Pope Pius V in Benediction, by a follower of Bartolomeo Passarotti, 16th century. The Dominican pope always wore his white friar's habit—which is why popes still dress in white.

polycarp_of_smyrna_bishop.label: The mosaic
polycarp_of_smyrna_bishop.text: The Procession of the Holy Martyrs in Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, Ravenna, about 560. Polycarp walks among a line of white-robed martyrs carrying their crowns toward Christ.

pontian_i_pope_and_hippolytus_of_rome_pr.label: The altarpiece
pontian_i_pope_and_hippolytus_of_rome_pr.text: The Martyrdom of Saint Hippolytus by Dieric Bouts and Hugo van der Goes, about 1470–75. According to legend, Hippolytus was tied to four horses and torn apart. It is in St. Salvator's Cathedral, Bruges.

presentation_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.label: The painting
presentation_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.text: The Presentation of the Virgin by Titian, 1534–38. The little girl climbs the Temple steps alone, watched by a crowd of Venetians. It still hangs in the room it was painted for, the Sala dell'Albergo of the old Scuola della Carità, now part of the Accademia Galleries, Venice.

presentation_of_the_lord.label: The painting
presentation_of_the_lord.text: The Presentation in the Temple by Andrea Mantegna, about 1454. The figures at the edges may be Mantegna himself and his wife Nicolosia, sister of Giovanni Bellini. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

queenship_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.label: The painting
queenship_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.text: The Coronation of the Virgin by Diego Velázquez, 1635–36, painted for the queen's oratory in the Alcázar of Madrid. The Father, Son and Spirit crown Mary in heaven. It is in the Museo del Prado.

raymond_of_penyafort_priest.label: The painting
raymond_of_penyafort_priest.text: The Virgin and Child with Saint Barbara and Saint Raymond of Penyafort, by Orazio Samacchini, painted on copper in 16th-century Bologna. Raymond is said to have sailed home from Majorca on his own cloak. It is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Chartres.

rita_of_cascia_religious.label: The painting
rita_of_cascia_religious.text: Saint Rita of Cascia by Antonio de Torres, Mexico, about 1720. Rita bears the wound of a thorn on her forehead, received while praying before a crucifix. It is in the El Paso Museum of Art.

robert_bellarmine_bishop.label: The painting
robert_bellarmine_bishop.text: Cardinal Robert Bellarmine, painted around 1622, the year after his death. It hangs in the Museum Plantin-Moretus in Antwerp, once the most important printing house in Europe.

romuald_of_ravenna_abbot.label: The painting
romuald_of_ravenna_abbot.text: Saint Romuald by Fra Angelico, about 1440, a small panel from the high altarpiece of San Marco in Florence. The founder of the Camaldolese hermits wears their white habit. It is in the Minneapolis Institute of Art.

rose_of_lima_virgin.label: The painting
rose_of_lima_virgin.text: Saint Rose of Lima, attributed to José del Pozo, about 1810–20. The first saint of the Americas wears her crown of roses, beneath which she hid a band of spikes. It is in the Lima Art Museum.

scholastica_of_nursia_virgin.label: The painting
scholastica_of_nursia_virgin.text: Saint Scholastica Obtaining a Storm from Heaven by Louis Galloche, 1706. Her prayer brings the thunderstorm that kept her brother Benedict from leaving. It is in the Musée Carnavalet, Paris.

sebastian_of_milan_martyr.label: The painting
sebastian_of_milan_martyr.text: Saint Sebastian by Andrea Mantegna, about 1457–59. Pierced with arrows, he stands against a ruined Roman arch; Mantegna signed his name in Greek on the pillar, and a horseman hides in the clouds. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

seven_holy_founders_of_the_servite_order.label: The painting
seven_holy_founders_of_the_servite_order.text: The Madonna with the Seven Founders of the Servite Order by Agostino Masucci, 1728. The Virgin appears in glory to the seven Florentine founders, kneeling in their black habits. It is in the Art Institute of Chicago.

simon_and_jude_apostles.label: The painting
simon_and_jude_apostles.text: The Martyrdom of Saints Simon and Jude by Stefan Lochner, about 1435, one of his panels of the deaths of the apostles. Tradition says the two preached together in Persia and were killed there. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.

sixtus_ii_pope_and_companions_martyrs.label: The painting
sixtus_ii_pope_and_companions_martyrs.text: The Sistine Madonna by Raphael, about 1512, painted for the church of San Sisto in Piacenza. Pope Sixtus II kneels at left, his tiara set on the ledge; the two famous cherubs lean on the frame below. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

stanislaus_of_szczepanow_bishop.label: The painting
stanislaus_of_szczepanow_bishop.text: The Death of Bishop Stanisław by Józef Peszka, early 1800s. King Bolesław II, excommunicated by the bishop, kills him at the altar in 1079. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.

stephen_i_of_hungary.label: The painting
stephen_i_of_hungary.text: Saint Stephen of Hungary Receiving the Papal Legate by Pieter Jozef Verhaghen, 1770. The pope's envoy brings the crown for Hungary's first king. It is in the Hungarian National Gallery, Budapest.

stephen_the_first_martyr.label: The painting
stephen_the_first_martyr.text: The Sermon of Saint Stephen by Vittore Carpaccio, 1514, painted for the confraternity of St. Stephen in Venice. Turbaned listeners sit in an imaginary Jerusalem. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

sylvester_i_pope.label: The painting
sylvester_i_pope.text: The Legend of Saint Sylvester by Agnolo Gaddi, about 1380–85. Legend tells how the pope tamed a dragon that was poisoning Rome. It is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

teresa_of_calcutta_virgin.label: The painting
teresa_of_calcutta_virgin.text: Mother Teresa by the Indian artist Rajasekharan Parameswaran. She wears the white sari with blue stripes, the dress of the poorest women of Calcutta, which she chose as the habit of her sisters.

teresa_of_jesus_of_avila_virgin.label: The painting
teresa_of_jesus_of_avila_virgin.text: Saint Teresa of Avila Interceding for Souls in Purgatory by Peter Paul Rubens. Teresa kneels before the risen Christ to plead for the souls in purgatory, as angels lift them from the flames below. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

thanksgiving_day.label: The painting
thanksgiving_day.text: Thanksgiving at Plymouth by Jennie Augusta Brownscombe, 1925, her second version of a scene she first painted in 1914. It is in the National Museum of Women in the Arts, Washington.

therese_of_the_child_jesus_and_the_holy_.label: The photograph
therese_of_the_child_jesus_and_the_holy_.text: Thérèse in the cloister of the Lisieux Carmel, photographed by her sister Céline in 1896, a year before she died. She holds a parchment with words of St. Teresa of Ávila: 'I would give a thousand lives to save one soul.'

thomas_apostle.label: The painting
thomas_apostle.text: The Incredulity of Saint Thomas by Caravaggio, about 1601–02. Christ guides Thomas's finger into the wound in his side as two apostles lean in. It is in the Sanssouci Picture Gallery, Potsdam.

thomas_aquinas_priest.label: The painting
thomas_aquinas_priest.text: The Apotheosis of Saint Thomas Aquinas by Francisco de Zurbarán, 1631, one of his largest paintings, made for the Dominican college of St. Thomas in Seville. Thomas rises among the Doctors of the Church as the emperor Charles V kneels below. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Seville.

thomas_becket_bishop.label: The painting
thomas_becket_bishop.text: The Martyrdom of Saint Thomas Becket by Jean-Baptiste Marie Pierre, 1748. The king's knights strike down the archbishop in Canterbury Cathedral. It is in the church of Notre-Dame-de-la-Nativité de Bercy, Paris.

timothy_of_ephesus_and_titus_of_crete_bi.label: The icon
timothy_of_ephesus_and_titus_of_crete_bi.text: The Saints of the 22nd of January by Konstantinos Tzanes, a Cretan painter working in 17th-century Venice. It belongs to the Hellenic Institute of Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Studies, Venice.

transfiguration_of_the_lord.label: The painting
transfiguration_of_the_lord.text: The Transfiguration by Raphael, 1516–20, his last painting. Above, Christ shines on the mountain; below, the disciples struggle to heal a possessed boy. It was hung above his body at his funeral. It is in the Vatican Pinacoteca.

turibius_of_mogrovejo_bishop.label: The painting
turibius_of_mogrovejo_bishop.text: Saint Toribio Alfonso de Mogrovejo, Archbishop of Lima, a 17th-century Spanish painting. He walked thousands of miles across the Andes to visit every corner of his diocese. It is in the National Museum of Fine Arts, Buenos Aires.

vincent_de_paul_priest.label: The painting
vincent_de_paul_priest.text: Vincent de Paul by Simon François de Tours, the portrait painted in his lifetime and the best-known likeness of him. His kindly, weathered face became the image of charity in France.

vincent_ferrer_priest.label: The painting
vincent_ferrer_priest.text: Saint Vincent Ferrer by Francesco del Cossa, 1472–73, the center of the Griffoni altarpiece for San Petronio in Bologna. The preacher of the Last Judgment points to Christ above. It is in the National Gallery, London.

vincent_of_saragossa_deacon.label: The painting
vincent_of_saragossa_deacon.text: Saints Vincent, James and Eustace by Antonio and Piero del Pollaiuolo, 1467–68, made for the Chapel of the Cardinal of Portugal at San Miniato al Monte, Florence. It is in the Uffizi; a copy stands in the chapel.

visitation_of_mary.label: The painting
visitation_of_mary.text: The Visitation by Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1491. Elizabeth kneels before Mary under a classical arch, as Mary Jacobi and Mary Salome look on. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

wenceslaus_i_of_bohemia_martyr.label: The statue
wenceslaus_i_of_bohemia_martyr.text: The Saint Wenceslas Monument by Josef Václav Myslbek, completed in 1912, at the top of Wenceslas Square in Prague. It has been the city's great rallying point, where crowds gathered in 1918, 1968 and 1989.

ash_wednesday.label: The painting
ash_wednesday.text: Christ in the Wilderness by Ivan Kramskoi, 1872. Christ sits alone among stones at dawn, his hands clenched, after forty days of fasting. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

palm_sunday_of_the_passion_of_the_lord.label: The painting
palm_sunday_of_the_passion_of_the_lord.text: Christ's Entry into Jerusalem by Adriaen van Nieulandt, 1655. A great crowd pours along the road, spreading cloaks and branches before Christ as he rides into the city. It is in the National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen.

thursday_of_the_lords_supper.label: The painting
thursday_of_the_lords_supper.text: The Last Supper by Leonardo da Vinci, 1495–98, on the refectory wall of Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan. Leonardo shows the moment Jesus says 'One of you will betray me.' His experimental technique began flaking within his lifetime.

friday_of_the_passion_of_the_lord.label: The painting
friday_of_the_passion_of_the_lord.text: Christ Crucified by Diego Velázquez, about 1632, painted for the convent of San Plácido in Madrid. Alone against a dark background, it inspired a book-length poem by Miguel de Unamuno. It is in the Museo del Prado.

holy_saturday.label: The painting
holy_saturday.text: The Entombment of Christ by Caravaggio, 1603–04, painted for the Chiesa Nuova in Rome. Nicodemus and John lower the body as the women grieve. Napoleon took it to Paris; it came back after his fall and is in the Vatican Pinacoteca.

divine_mercy_sunday.label: The painting
divine_mercy_sunday.text: The original Divine Mercy image by Eugeniusz Kazimirowski, 1934, painted in Vilnius under St. Faustina's own direction. It hangs in the Divine Mercy Sanctuary in Vilnius, Lithuania.

season_ADVENT_1.label: The fresco
season_ADVENT_1.text: The Prophet Isaiah by Michelangelo, 1508–12, on the Sistine Chapel ceiling. Isaiah turns from his book at an angel's call—the prophet of Advent, who foretold that a virgin would bear a son called Emmanuel.

season_ADVENT_2.label: The painting
season_ADVENT_2.text: The Appearance of Christ Before the People by Alexander Ivanov, 1837–57, a canvas more than seven meters wide that took him twenty years. John the Baptist points to the distant figure of Christ: 'Prepare the way of the Lord.' It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

season_ADVENT_3.label: The painting
season_ADVENT_3.text: The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds by Thomas Cole, 1833–34, founder of the Hudson River School. The angel's light breaks over a vast moonlit landscape. It is in the Chrysler Museum of Art, Norfolk, Virginia.

season_CHRISTMAS_TIME_1.label: The painting
season_CHRISTMAS_TIME_1.text: The Adoration of the Shepherds by Giorgione, about 1505–10, known as the Allendale Nativity. Two shepherds kneel at the mouth of a cave in a wide Venetian landscape. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

season_CHRISTMAS_TIME_2.label: The painting
season_CHRISTMAS_TIME_2.text: The Flight into Egypt by Titian, about 1508, one of his earliest works. The Holy Family hurries through a landscape full of animals, led by a young angel. It is in the Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.

season_LENT_1.label: The painting
season_LENT_1.text: Christ in the Wilderness by Moretto da Brescia, about 1515–20. Christ sits alone among wild animals, as Mark's Gospel says, 'and the angels ministered to him.' It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

season_LENT_2.label: The painting
season_LENT_2.text: The Return of the Prodigal Son by Rembrandt, about 1668, painted near the end of his life. The ragged son kneels with his head against his father's chest, and the father's two hands rest on his back. It is in the Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.

season_LENT_3.label: The painting
season_LENT_3.text: The Agony in the Garden by Giovanni Bellini, about 1458–60. Christ prays on a rock as dawn breaks and the disciples sleep; Judas and the soldiers are already on their way. It is in the National Gallery, London.

season_PASCHAL_TRIDUUM_1.label: The painting
season_PASCHAL_TRIDUUM_1.text: Christ Crucified by Diego Velázquez, about 1632, painted for the convent of San Plácido in Madrid. Alone against a dark background, it inspired a book-length poem by Miguel de Unamuno. It is in the Museo del Prado.

season_EASTER_TIME_1.label: The painting
season_EASTER_TIME_1.text: Noli me tangere by Titian, about 1514. Mary Magdalene reaches toward the risen Christ, who draws back: 'Do not cling to me.' It is in the National Gallery, London.

season_EASTER_TIME_2.label: The painting
season_EASTER_TIME_2.text: The Supper at Emmaus, 1853, in the abbey church of Saint-Étienne in Caen, Normandy, founded by William the Conqueror. The two disciples recognize Jesus in the breaking of the bread.

season_EASTER_TIME_3.label: The painting
season_EASTER_TIME_3.text: Christ Appearing to the Apostles after the Resurrection by Szymon Czechowicz, an 18th-century Polish painter trained in Rome. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.

season_ORDINARY_TIME_1.label: The icon
season_ORDINARY_TIME_1.text: Christ Pantocrator from St. Catherine's Monastery, Sinai, painted in wax in the 500s, one of the oldest icons in the world. The two sides of the face differ, showing Christ as both judge and merciful savior.

season_ORDINARY_TIME_2.label: The painting
season_ORDINARY_TIME_2.text: The Sermon on the Mount by Jan Brueghel the Elder, 1598, painted on copper. A huge crowd in Flemish dress gathers on a hillside to hear Christ. It is in the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles.

season_ORDINARY_TIME_3.label: The mosaic
season_ORDINARY_TIME_3.text: The Good Shepherd, a mosaic of about 425–450 in the Mausoleum of Galla Placidia, Ravenna, one of the oldest and best-preserved Christian mosaics. A young, golden-robed Christ sits among his sheep beneath a deep blue vault of stars. 'I am the good shepherd.'

season_ORDINARY_TIME_4.label: The painting
season_ORDINARY_TIME_4.text: The Good Samaritan by Théodule Ribot, 1870, a French realist known for his dark, Spanish-inspired style. It is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Pau.

season_ORDINARY_TIME_5.label: The painting
season_ORDINARY_TIME_5.text: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee by Rembrandt, 1633, his only seascape. It was stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston in 1990 and has never been found; its empty frame still hangs there.

season_ORDINARY_TIME_6.label: The painting
season_ORDINARY_TIME_6.text: The Wedding at Cana by Paolo Veronese, 1562–63, the largest painting in the Louvre. Napoleon's troops took it from the refectory of San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice; it now faces the Mona Lisa.

season_ORDINARY_TIME_7.label: The painting
season_ORDINARY_TIME_7.text: The Light of the World by William Holman Hunt. Christ knocks at an overgrown door that has no handle on the outside. This large final version, finished in 1904, toured the world and now hangs in St. Paul's Cathedral, London.

season_ORDINARY_TIME_8.label: The painting
season_ORDINARY_TIME_8.text: Christ Healing the Paralytic by Anthony van Dyck and his workshop, about 1621. 'Rise, take up your mat, and walk.'

season_ORDINARY_TIME_9.label: The painting
season_ORDINARY_TIME_9.text: The Calling of Peter and Andrew by Duccio, 1308–11, a panel from the back of his great Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

season_ORDINARY_TIME_10.label: The painting
season_ORDINARY_TIME_10.text: The Multiplication of the Loaves and Fishes by Paolo Farinati, in the church of San Giorgio in Braida, Verona. Five loaves and two fish feed five thousand.

day_of_prayer_for_the_legal_protection_o.label: The painting
day_of_prayer_for_the_legal_protection_o.text: The Visitation by Alonso Cano, painter, sculptor and architect of 17th-century Granada. Mary, newly expecting Jesus, greets her cousin Elizabeth, whose child leapt in her womb at the sound of her voice. Joseph and Zechariah stand behind them. It is in the Musée Goya, Castres, France.

andre_bessette_religious.label: The photograph
andre_bessette_religious.text: Brother André as an old man. For forty years the humble doorman of a Montreal school, he became famous for healings, and the crutches left by pilgrims still line the walls of St. Joseph's Oratory, the great basilica he inspired.

andrew_kim_tae_gon_priest_paul_chong_ha_.label: The painting
andrew_kim_tae_gon_priest_paul_chong_ha_.text: Andrew Kim Taegon, from an oil portrait by the Korean painter Louis Chang, about 1920. Kim was the first Korean-born priest; he was beheaded near Seoul in 1846 at twenty-five.

anthony_mary_claret_bishop.label: The photograph
anthony_mary_claret_bishop.text: Anthony Mary Claret around 1860, when he was confessor to Queen Isabella II of Spain. Earlier, as Archbishop of Santiago de Cuba, he survived an assassination attempt.

anthony_zaccaria_priest.label: The painting
anthony_zaccaria_priest.text: Saint Anthony Zaccaria holds the rule of his Barnabites, a lily for purity and a scourge for penance. He began as a doctor in Cremona before becoming a priest.

callistus_i_pope.label: The fresco
callistus_i_pope.text: Pope Callistus I, a portrait from the great series of papal portraits on the walls of the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls, Rome, begun in the 5th century. It survived the fire that destroyed the basilica in 1823.

christopher_magallanes_priest_and_compan.label: The photograph
christopher_magallanes_priest_and_compan.text: Father Cristóbal Magallanes, shot in 1927 during the Cristero persecution in Mexico. He forgave his executioners before he died.

cornelius_i_pope_and_cyprian_of_carthage.label: The painting
cornelius_i_pope_and_cyprian_of_carthage.text: Saint Cyprian by the Master of Messkirch, about 1535–40, from the side altars of St. Martin's Church in Messkirch. It is in the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart.

damien_de_veuster_priest.label: The photograph
damien_de_veuster_priest.text: Father Damien, photographed by William Brigham at Kalaupapa in 1889, weeks before he died of leprosy. He had lived among the patients of Molokai for sixteen years, and his face shows the disease he caught serving them.

faustina_kowalska_virgin.label: The photograph
faustina_kowalska_virgin.text: Sister Faustina in Płock, 1931, the year Jesus first appeared to her there as the Divine Mercy and asked her to have his image painted.

frances_xavier_cabrini_virgin.label: The photograph
frances_xavier_cabrini_virgin.text: Mother Cabrini around 1900. She crossed the Atlantic more than twenty times and founded sixty-seven schools, orphanages and hospitals; she was the first U.S. citizen to be canonized.

francis_xavier_seelos_priest.label: The photograph
francis_xavier_seelos_priest.text: Francis Xavier Seelos around 1855. The Bavarian Redemptorist preached across America and died in New Orleans in 1867, nursing victims of yellow fever.

john_bosco_priest.label: The photograph
john_bosco_priest.text: Don Bosco in Turin, 1880, one of many photographs taken of him—he was among the first saints to be photographed often, and used pictures to promote his work for poor boys.

john_eudes_priest.label: The painting
john_eudes_priest.text: Saint John Eudes, a 17th-century portrait. The Norman missionary was the first to write a Mass in honor of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary.

john_nepomucene_neumann_bishop.label: The engraving
john_nepomucene_neumann_bishop.text: Bishop John Neumann, engraved by Samuel Hollyer, 1892. The Bohemian immigrant became Bishop of Philadelphia and built the first diocesan Catholic school system in America. It is in the Library of Congress.

john_paul_ii_pope.label: The photograph
john_paul_ii_pope.text: Pope John Paul II in October 1980, two years into his pontificate. Elected in 1978 as the first non-Italian pope in 455 years, he visited 129 countries and was canonized nine years after his death.

john_xxiii_pope.label: The portrait
john_xxiii_pope.text: Pope John XXIII, from a portrait of 1958–63. Expected to be a short 'caretaker' pope at seventy-six, he surprised the world by calling the Second Vatican Council.

josephine_bakhita_virgin.label: The photograph
josephine_bakhita_virgin.text: Josephine Bakhita in her religious habit. Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold into slavery, she was so traumatized she forgot her own name; 'Bakhita', meaning 'fortunate', was given by her captors.

junipero_serra_priest.label: The engraving
junipero_serra_priest.text: Junípero Serra, from the 1787 biography by his companion Francisco Palóu, the earliest known likeness. He founded the first nine of California's twenty-one missions.

justin_martyr.label: The fresco
justin_martyr.text: Saint Justin the Philosopher by Theophanes the Cretan, about 1546, on Mount Athos. Justin is shown with a scroll, as the first great Christian philosopher.

kateri_tekakwitha_virgin.label: The painting
kateri_tekakwitha_virgin.text: Kateri Tekakwitha, after the portrait attributed to Father Claude Chauchetière, the Jesuit who knew her at Kahnawake—the earliest known image of her, painted in the years after her death in 1680.

katharine_drexel_virgin.label: The photograph
katharine_drexel_virgin.text: Mother Katharine Drexel around 1915. Heiress to a Philadelphia banking fortune, she gave about twenty million dollars to found schools for Native American and Black students, including Xavier University in New Orleans.

lawrence_ruiz_and_companions_martyrs.label: The window
lawrence_ruiz_and_companions_martyrs.text: Lorenzo Ruiz in stained glass at Cubao Cathedral, Quezon City. A Manila calligrapher and father of three, he fled to Japan and was martyred at Nagasaki in 1637, the first Filipino saint.

louis_grignion_de_montfort_priest.label: The portrait
louis_grignion_de_montfort_priest.text: Louis de Montfort, a late 19th-century portrait. His book True Devotion to Mary was lost for over a century and found in a chest in 1842; John Paul II took his motto 'Totus tuus' from it.

marcellinus_of_rome_and_peter_the_exorci.label: The image
marcellinus_of_rome_and_peter_the_exorci.text: Saint Marcellinus, from Seligenstadt, Germany. In 827 Charlemagne's biographer Einhard brought the relics of Marcellinus and Peter from Rome to Seligenstadt, where they still rest in the basilica he built.

maria_goretti_virgin.label: The painting
maria_goretti_virgin.text: Maria Goretti by Giuseppe Brovelli-Soffredini, 1929. No photograph of her existed, so the painter worked from her mother's descriptions. Her mother lived to attend her canonization in 1950.

marianne_cope_virgin.label: The photograph
marianne_cope_virgin.text: Mother Marianne Cope, who in 1883 led six Franciscan sisters from Syracuse, New York, to care for leprosy patients in Hawaii. She nursed Father Damien in his last days and never caught the disease.

marie_rose_durocher_virgin.label: The painting
marie_rose_durocher_virgin.text: Marie-Rose Durocher, a copy of the portrait by Théophile Hamel. She founded the Sisters of the Holy Names of Jesus and Mary in Quebec to teach poor children.

martin_de_porres_religious.label: The painting
martin_de_porres_religious.text: A 17th-century portrait of Martin de Porres in the monastery of Santa Rosa de las Monjas in Lima, one of the earliest images of him. He carries a broom, the sign of his humble work.

maximilian_mary_raymund_kolbe_priest.label: The photograph
maximilian_mary_raymund_kolbe_priest.text: Father Maximilian Kolbe in 1936, the year he returned from founding a friary near Nagasaki. Five years later in Auschwitz he took the place of a condemned father of a family.

miguel_agustin_pro_priest.label: The photograph
miguel_agustin_pro_priest.text: Father Miguel Pro on the day of his arrest in 1927, in the civilian clothes he wore to minister in secret. The government photographed his execution to deter others; instead the pictures made him a hero.

our_lady_of_fatima.label: The image
our_lady_of_fatima.text: Our Lady of Fátima, as she is honored at the shrine in Portugal where she appeared to three shepherd children in 1917. The crown of the shrine's statue holds the bullet that struck John Paul II in 1981.

paul_of_the_cross_priest.label: The engraving
paul_of_the_cross_priest.text: Saint Paul of the Cross, engraved by G. B. Leonetti after a painting by A. Tofanelli. The founder of the Passionists preached the Passion of Christ across Italy. It is in the Wellcome Collection, London.

paul_vi_pope.label: The photograph
paul_vi_pope.text: Pope Paul VI, an official portrait of 1969. He completed the Second Vatican Council and was the first pope to fly in an airplane and visit five continents.

peter_chanel_priest.label: The illustration
peter_chanel_priest.text: Peter Chanel as a young man, from his 1885 biography. He became the first martyr of Oceania, killed on the island of Futuna in 1841; within a year the island was Christian.

peter_claver_priest.label: The painting
peter_claver_priest.text: Saint Peter Claver, a painting in the Palace of the Inquisition in Cartagena, Colombia. He stands by the harbor walls with a bowl of water, baptizing one of the enslaved. He met every slave ship arriving at Cartagena, and called himself ‘the slave of the slaves forever.’

peter_damian_bishop.label: The painting
