peter_damian_bishop.text: Saint Peter Damian by the anonymous Master of San Pier Damiani, about 1440–60. The hermit-cardinal wears the white habit of the Camaldolese.

peter_julian_eymard_priest.label: The image
peter_julian_eymard_priest.text: Saint Peter Julian Eymard, called the Apostle of the Eucharist. He founded the Blessed Sacrament Fathers in Paris to keep perpetual adoration.

pius_francesco_forgione_priest.label: The photograph
pius_francesco_forgione_priest.text: Padre Pio around 1947. He bore the stigmata for fifty years and drew crowds to the friary of San Giovanni Rotondo, where he heard confessions for up to sixteen hours a day.

pius_x_pope.label: The photograph
pius_x_pope.text: Pope Pius X, photographed by Ernest Walter Histed. The son of a village postman, he lowered the age of first communion so that children could receive it.

rose_philippine_duchesne_virgin.label: The portrait
rose_philippine_duchesne_virgin.text: Rose Philippine Duchesne, who founded the first house of the Society of the Sacred Heart in America in 1818. At seventy-one she went to live among the Potawatomi, who called her 'woman who prays always.'

sharbel_makhluf_priest.label: The image
sharbel_makhluf_priest.text: The traditional image of Saint Charbel, his face shadowed by his monk's hood. No photograph from his lifetime is known; this face became famous after a photograph taken at his monastery of Annaya in 1950.

teresa_benedicta_of_the_cross_stein_virg.label: The photograph
teresa_benedicta_of_the_cross_stein_virg.text: Edith Stein around 1938–39, the 'passport photo' taken at the Cologne Carmel before she fled to the Netherlands. In 1942 the Nazis arrested her there and she died at Auschwitz.

charles_lwanga_and_companions_martyrs.label: The photograph
charles_lwanga_and_companions_martyrs.text: The Basilica of the Uganda Martyrs at Namugongo, built in the shape of a traditional Ganda hut over the place where Charles Lwanga was burned to death in 1886. Every June 3, more than a million pilgrims walk there, many of them for days, from across East Africa.

advent_1_sunday_c.label: The fresco
advent_1_sunday_c.text: The Last Judgment by Michelangelo, 1536–41, covering the whole altar wall of the Sistine Chapel. Christ raises his arm in judgment as the dead rise and the saints crowd around him; it took Michelangelo five years.

advent_2_sunday_c.label: The painting
advent_2_sunday_c.text: Saint John the Baptist by Titian, about 1540, a powerful figure of the prophet in the wilderness with his lamb beside him. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.

advent_3_sunday_c.label: The painting
advent_3_sunday_c.text: The Preaching of Saint John the Baptist by Rembrandt, about 1634–35, painted in shades of brown as a study. A great crowd of every kind of listener, some rapt, some bored, gathers around the prophet. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

advent_4_sunday_c.label: The painting
advent_4_sunday_c.text: The Visitation by Jacopo Pontormo, about 1528–29. Mary and Elizabeth embrace in a swirl of brilliant color, watched by two women who seem to be their own doubles. It is in the church of San Michele at Carmignano, near Florence.

lent_1_sunday_b.label: The fresco
lent_1_sunday_b.text: The Temptations of Christ by Sandro Botticelli, 1481–82, on the wall of the Sistine Chapel. The devil, disguised as a hermit, tempts Christ three times in the background, while in front a priest performs a sacrifice at the Temple.

lent_2_sunday_b.label: The fresco
lent_2_sunday_b.text: The Transfiguration by Fra Angelico, about 1440, painted on the wall of a friar's cell in the convent of San Marco, Florence. Christ stands with arms outstretched in a blaze of white light, foreshadowing the cross.

lent_3_sunday_b.label: The painting
lent_3_sunday_b.text: Christ Driving the Traders from the Temple by El Greco, about 1600. He painted the subject again and again over his career; Christ swings the whip in the middle of a tangle of falling bodies and overturned tables.

lent_4_sunday_b.label: The painting
lent_4_sunday_b.text: Nicodemus Visiting Jesus by Henry Ossawa Tanner, 1899, painted after his first journey to the Holy Land. They talk by night on a rooftop in Jerusalem. Tanner was the first African American painter to win international fame. It is in the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts.

lent_5_sunday_b.label: The altarpiece
lent_5_sunday_b.text: The Crucifixion from the Isenheim Altarpiece by Matthias Grünewald, 1512–16, painted for a monastery hospital that cared for victims of a terrible skin disease. Christ's body bears their sores. It is in the Unterlinden Museum, Colmar, France.

easter_time_4_sunday_b.label: The painting
easter_time_4_sunday_b.text: The Good Shepherd by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1660, showing Christ as a gentle child shepherd with his hand on a lamb, ruined columns behind him. It is in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.

easter_time_5_sunday_b.label: The engraving
easter_time_5_sunday_b.text: Christ the True Vine, an old engraving. Christ hangs on a cross that grows into a vine, and its branches hold the apostles and evangelists, above the words 'I am the vine, you are the branches.' It is in the Wellcome Collection, London.

easter_time_6_sunday_b.label: The painting
easter_time_6_sunday_b.text: The Last Supper by Juan de Juanes, about 1562, the most famous of Valencia's Renaissance painters. Christ holds up the host as the apostles gather close; Judas, in the foreground, clutches the purse. It is in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.

ordinary_time_2_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_2_sunday_b.text: Ecce Agnus Dei by Dieric Bouts, about 1462–64. John the Baptist points out Jesus walking past to a kneeling donor: 'Behold the Lamb of God.' It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.

ordinary_time_3_sunday_b.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_3_sunday_b.text: The Calling of the First Apostles by Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1481, on the wall of the Sistine Chapel. Peter and Andrew kneel before Christ on the shore of Galilee, while in the distance Jesus calls James and John from their boat.

ordinary_time_12_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_12_sunday_b.text: Christ on the Sea of Galilee by Eugène Delacroix, 1841. Waves toss the little boat as the disciples panic and Christ sleeps peacefully in the stern. Delacroix painted the subject many times. It is in the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.

ordinary_time_13_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_13_sunday_b.text: The Raising of Jairus's Daughter by Ilya Repin, 1871, painted at twenty-seven for the gold medal of the St. Petersburg Academy, which he won. It is in the State Russian Museum.

ordinary_time_15_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_15_sunday_b.text: The Exhortation to the Apostles by James Tissot, 1886–94, from his series of 350 scenes of the life of Christ, painted after years of travel in the Holy Land. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.

ordinary_time_17_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_17_sunday_b.text: The Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes by Jacopo Tintoretto, about 1545–50. The crowd spreads across a wide landscape as the bread is passed out. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_18_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_18_sunday_b.text: The Saviour with the Eucharist by Juan de Juanes, about 1545–50, once the door of the tabernacle on a Valencian high altar. Christ holds up the host and chalice. It is in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.

ordinary_time_19_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_19_sunday_b.text: The Last Supper by Dieric Bouts, 1464–68, the center of his Altarpiece of the Holy Sacrament, commissioned by a Eucharistic confraternity. Christ blesses the host. It still hangs in St. Peter's Church in Leuven, Belgium, where it was made.

ordinary_time_24_sunday_b.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_24_sunday_b.text: The Delivery of the Keys by Pietro Perugino, 1481–82, on the wall of the Sistine Chapel. Christ gives the keys of the kingdom to the kneeling Peter, in a vast piazza before an ideal temple.

ordinary_time_27_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_27_sunday_b.text: Christ Blessing the Children by Lucas Cranach the Elder, painted after 1537, one of several versions from his workshop. Mothers crowd around Jesus with their babies. It is in the National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen.

ordinary_time_28_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_28_sunday_b.text: Christ and the Rich Young Ruler by Heinrich Hofmann, 1889, one of the best-loved religious paintings of its time. Jesus points the young man to the poor at his side. It hangs in Riverside Church, New York.

ordinary_time_29_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_29_sunday_b.text: Christ and the Sons of Zebedee by Ambrosius Francken the Elder, 1610, a wing of the altarpiece of St. James's Church in Antwerp. Their mother asks for places of honor for her sons, James and John.

ordinary_time_30_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_30_sunday_b.text: Christ Healing the Blind by El Greco, about 1570, painted in Venice before he settled in Spain. Christ touches the blind man's eyes in a deep Italian piazza. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_33_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_33_sunday_b.text: The Last Judgment by Hans Memling, about 1467–71. The archangel Michael weighs souls as the dead rise. It was captured by a pirate ship on its way to Florence and has been in Gdańsk, Poland, ever since.

holy_tuesday.label: The painting
holy_tuesday.text: The Last Supper by Philippe de Champaigne, the painter of the abbey of Port-Royal, in the mid-1600s. The apostles turn to one another at the moment Jesus says, 'One of you will betray me.' This version is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Lyon.

holy_wednesday.label: The painting
holy_wednesday.text: Judas Returning the Thirty Pieces of Silver by Rembrandt, 1629, painted when he was twenty-three. Too late, Judas throws the coins down before the priests and elders, wringing his hands in despair.

ordinary_time_4_sunday_b.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_4_sunday_b.text: Jesus Healing a Man Possessed by a Devil, by Gustave Doré, from his illustrated Bible of 1866. Doré's 241 Bible engravings were reprinted around the world and shaped how generations pictured the Gospels.

ordinary_time_5_sunday_b.label: The illumination
ordinary_time_5_sunday_b.text: Jesus and Peter's Mother-in-Law, from the Hitda Codex, a Gospel book made in Cologne around 1020 for Abbess Hitda of Meschede. Christ takes the sick woman by the hand. It is in the University and State Library, Darmstadt.

easter_time_3_sunday_b.label: The painting
easter_time_3_sunday_b.text: The Appearance While the Apostles Are at Table by Duccio, 1308–11, a small panel from his Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral. The risen Christ appears among the startled disciples at their meal. It is in the Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Siena.

ordinary_time_10_sunday_b.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_10_sunday_b.text: Jesus Preaching to the Multitude by Gustave Doré, from his illustrated Bible of 1866. Crowds press around Jesus to listen, as they did in the house at Capernaum.

ordinary_time_11_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_11_sunday_b.text: Head of Christ by Rembrandt, about 1648–56, one of a series of small studies he painted from a young Jewish man of Amsterdam. Gentle and searching, it broke with centuries of idealized portraits of Jesus. It is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

ordinary_time_14_sunday_b.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_14_sunday_b.text: Christ in the Synagogue by Gustave Doré, from his illustrated Bible of 1866. Jesus teaches in the synagogue as the elders look on, as he did in his hometown of Nazareth, where they asked, 'Is he not the carpenter?'

ordinary_time_16_sunday_b.label: The etching
ordinary_time_16_sunday_b.text: The Hundred Guilder Print by Rembrandt, about 1649, his most famous etching. Christ stands in the middle of a crowd of the sick, the poor and the curious, welcoming them all. Its nickname comes from the then-record price it fetched. This impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_21_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_21_sunday_b.text: Christ's Charge to Peter by Raphael, 1515–16, a design for one of the tapestries he made for the Sistine Chapel. Peter kneels with the keys before the risen Christ, as the other apostles watch. The full-size design is in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

ordinary_time_22_sunday_b.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_22_sunday_b.text: Jesus and the Pharisees by Gustave Doré. The Pharisees press Jesus with questions in a narrow street, trying to catch him out. Doré made hundreds of Bible engravings, reprinted around the world.

ordinary_time_23_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_23_sunday_b.text: Christ Giving His Blessing by Hans Memling, 1478. Christ looks straight out at the viewer and raises his hand in blessing, as if speaking the healing word 'Ephphatha'. It is in the Norton Simon Museum, Pasadena, California.

ordinary_time_25_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_25_sunday_b.text: Head of Christ by Correggio, about 1525–30, painted as if on Veronica's veil. Christ looks out at the viewer with quiet tenderness. It is in the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles.

ordinary_time_26_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_26_sunday_b.text: The Blessing Christ by Giovanni Bellini, about 1465–70. The risen Christ, his wounds visible, raises his hand in blessing against a dawn landscape. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

ordinary_time_31_sunday_b.label: The painting
ordinary_time_31_sunday_b.text: Salvator Mundi by Antonello da Messina, 1465, his earliest dated painting. Christ raises his hand in blessing and rests the other on a ledge; a first, discarded position of the hand is still visible. It is in the National Gallery, London.

ordinary_time_32_sunday_b.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_32_sunday_b.text: The Widow's Mite by Gustave Doré, from his illustrated Bible of 1866. A poor widow drops her two small coins into the Temple treasury as Jesus watches from the steps.

ordinary_time_33_sunday_a.label: The painting
ordinary_time_33_sunday_a.text: The Parable of the Talents by Willem de Poorter, a pupil of Rembrandt, about 1640s. A servant counts out his master's money by lamplight in a dark counting room.

advent_1_sunday_b.label: The watercolor
advent_1_sunday_b.text: The Wise and Foolish Virgins by William Blake, about 1822. At midnight the bridegroom's coming is announced by an angel with a trumpet; the wise virgins hold their lamps ready while the foolish beg for oil. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

advent_2_sunday_b.label: The painting
advent_2_sunday_b.text: The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1566. A crowd of every kind of person gathers in a forest clearing to hear John, and among them, near the center, stands Christ. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest.

advent_3_sunday_b.label: The painting
advent_3_sunday_b.text: Saint John the Baptist Preaching by Paolo Veronese, about 1562. John points toward a distant figure — Christ, 'the one among you whom you do not recognize.' It is in the Galleria Borghese, Rome.

advent_4_sunday_b.label: The altarpiece
advent_4_sunday_b.text: The Annunciation by Fra Angelico, about 1426, painted for a convent in Fiesole. On the left, Adam and Eve are driven out of Eden; under the loggia, Gabriel greets the new Eve. It is in the Prado Museum, Madrid.

advent_1_monday.label: The painting
advent_1_monday.text: Christ and the Centurion by Paolo Veronese, about 1571. The Roman officer kneels in armor before Christ, his soldiers around him, in a Venetian street. It is in the Prado Museum, Madrid.

advent_1_wednesday.label: The painting
advent_1_wednesday.text: The Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, 1670–74, painted for the church of the Hospital de la Caridad in Seville, a brotherhood that fed the poor. It still hangs there.

advent_1_thursday.label: The engraving
advent_1_thursday.text: The House Built on Rock, an engraving after Hendrick Goltzius, the great Dutch engraver of the late 1500s. The wise man's house stands firm on rock while the storm rages. It is in the North Holland Archives, Haarlem.

advent_1_saturday.label: The painting
advent_1_saturday.text: The Harvesters by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1565, one of his series of the months. 'The harvest is abundant': peasants cut and stack golden wheat and rest at noon under a pear tree. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

advent_3_tuesday.label: The engraving
advent_3_tuesday.text: The Parable of the Two Sons in the Vineyard, an engraving by Georg Pencz, about 1535, from his series The Story of Christ. Pencz was a pupil of Albrecht Dürer in Nuremberg. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

advent_3_wednesday.label: The painting
advent_3_wednesday.text: Saint John the Baptist in Prison Visited by Two Disciples by Giovanni di Paolo, 1455–60, one of a series of panels on John's life. John sends his disciples through the barred window to ask, 'Are you the one who is to come?' It is in the Art Institute of Chicago.

advent_december_17.label: The painting
advent_december_17.text: The Tree of Jesse, about 1500, from the circle of Geertgen tot Sint Jans in Haarlem. The kings of Israel sit in the branches of a tree growing from the sleeping Jesse, with the Virgin and Child at the top. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

advent_december_18.label: The painting
advent_december_18.text: The Dream of Saint Joseph by Gerard Seghers, about 1625–30. An angel rushes in to wake the sleeping Joseph and give him God's message, while Mary and the Child rest in the shadows behind. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

advent_december_19.label: The painting
advent_december_19.text: The Angel Appearing to Zacharias by William Blake, 1799–1800, one of the Bible paintings he made for his friend Thomas Butts. The priest stands by the golden lampstand in the Temple as Gabriel appears beside the altar of incense. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

advent_december_20.label: The painting
advent_december_20.text: The Annunciation by Jan van Eyck, about 1434–36. Gabriel greets Mary in a dim Romanesque church, and their words are written in gold between them; Mary's answer is painted upside down so that God can read it. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

advent_december_22.label: The painting
advent_december_22.text: The Madonna of the Magnificat by Sandro Botticelli, about 1483. Mary writes the words of her song in a book held by angels, while the Child guides her hand. It is in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.

christmas_octave_day_6.label: The painting
christmas_octave_day_6.text: An Old Woman Reading, probably the Prophetess Anna, by Rembrandt, 1631. Light falls on the old woman's hand resting on the page of Scripture. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

friday_after_epiphany.label: The illumination
friday_after_epiphany.text: The Cleansing of the Leper from the Codex Egberti, about 980, one of the earliest picture cycles of the life of Christ, painted at Reichenau for Archbishop Egbert of Trier. It is in the City Library of Trier.

saturday_after_epiphany.label: The painting
saturday_after_epiphany.text: Saint John the Baptist by Leonardo da Vinci, about 1513–16, probably his last painting. John smiles out of the darkness and points upward to the one who must increase. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

ordinary_time_1_tuesday.label: The etching
ordinary_time_1_tuesday.text: Christ Preaching, called 'La Petite Tombe', an etching by Rembrandt, about 1652. Listeners of every age crowd around Christ, who teaches 'as one having authority'. This impression is in the Cleveland Museum of Art.

ordinary_time_1_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_1_thursday.text: Christ and the Lepers by Gebhard Fugel, about 1920, a Bavarian painter of churches and Bible scenes. The lepers kneel at the roadside as Christ stops for them.

ordinary_time_1_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_1_saturday.text: The Feast in the House of Levi by Paolo Veronese, 1573, over 42 feet wide. Painted as a Last Supper, it was so crowded with dogs, jesters and soldiers that the Inquisition summoned Veronese; he simply renamed it after Levi's banquet. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.

ordinary_time_2_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_2_tuesday.text: August, by Marten van Valckenborch, about 1585, from a series of the months, each with a Gospel scene. In the harvest fields, Christ defends his disciples for picking grain on the sabbath.

ordinary_time_3_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_3_friday.text: Wheatfield with a Reaper by Vincent van Gogh, 1889, painted from his window at Saint-Rémy. 'When the grain is ripe, he wields the sickle at once.' Van Gogh wrote that he saw in the reaper an image of death, 'in the great book of nature'. It is in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_5_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_5_tuesday.text: Christ among the Pharisees by Jacob Jordaens, 17th century. The Pharisees press around Christ with their books of the Law, arguing over the traditions of the elders.

ordinary_time_7_wednesday.label: The icon
ordinary_time_7_wednesday.text: An Ethiopian triptych of the 15th century: Mary and her Son in the center, the apostles and saints on the wings. It is in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.

ordinary_time_8_monday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_8_monday.text: Christ Counsels the Rich Young Man, a 16th-century Netherlandish engraving. The young man, richly dressed, stands before Christ and the apostles. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_8_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_8_friday.text: Christ Driving the Money Changers from the Temple by Hubert Robert, 1760, the French painter of ruins and grand architecture. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

ordinary_time_10_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_10_tuesday.text: The Sermon on the Mount by Carl Bloch, 1877, one of 23 Gospel scenes he painted for the chapel of Frederiksborg Castle, Denmark.

ordinary_time_10_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_10_thursday.text: The Reconciliation of Jacob and Esau, 17th century, Flemish. The brothers embrace after twenty years of enmity — 'go first and be reconciled with your brother.' It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_10_saturday.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_10_saturday.text: The Sermon on the Mount by Fra Angelico, about 1440–42, painted on the wall of a friar's cell at the Convent of San Marco, Florence. The apostles sit in a ring on the bare rock around Christ.

ordinary_time_11_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_11_monday.text: The Mocking of Christ by Jacopo Bassano, 1560s. By night the soldiers crown Christ with thorns and strike him, and he does not resist: 'If any one strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.' It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.

ordinary_time_11_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_11_wednesday.text: An Old Woman Praying by Nicolaes Maes, about 1655, a pupil of Rembrandt. Alone at her table, among her Bible, hourglass and skull, she prays with folded hands.

ordinary_time_11_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_11_thursday.text: The Angelus by Jean-François Millet, 1857–59. At the sound of the distant church bell, two peasants stop work in the field to pray. It is in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

ordinary_time_11_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_11_friday.text: The Parable of the Rich Fool by Rembrandt, 1627, painted when he was 21. An old man examines a coin by candlelight among his ledgers and money bags. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

ordinary_time_12_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_12_wednesday.text: The Sermon on the Mount by Claude Lorrain, 1656. Christ teaches from a wooded hill that rises out of a wide, imagined Holy Land, with the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan below. It is in the Frick Collection, New York.

ordinary_time_12_friday.label: The drawing
ordinary_time_12_friday.text: Christ Heals a Leper, a Dutch drawing in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_12_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_12_saturday.text: The Centurion of Capernaum by Johannes Ykens, a 17th-century Flemish painter. The Roman officer bows before Christ: 'Lord, I am not worthy.'

ordinary_time_13_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_13_friday.text: The Calling of Saint Matthew by Hendrick ter Brugghen, 1621, a Dutch follower of Caravaggio. Matthew, at a table crowded with coins and tax collectors, points to himself: 'Me?' It is in the Centraal Museum, Utrecht.

ordinary_time_14_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_14_saturday.text: Christus Consolator by Ary Scheffer, 1837. Christ comforts the suffering of every age — a slave, a mourning mother, a prisoner — 'Do not be afraid.' It is in the Dordrechts Museum, the Netherlands.

ordinary_time_15_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_15_monday.text: The Seven Works of Mercy by Caravaggio, 1607, painted for a charitable brotherhood in Naples. In one dark street, a man gives a drink to the thirsty, a daughter feeds her imprisoned father, and the dead are carried out. It still hangs in the Pio Monte della Misericordia, Naples.

ordinary_time_16_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_16_monday.text: Jonah and the Whale by Pieter Lastman, 1621, Rembrandt's teacher. The great fish spits Jonah onto the shore after three days and three nights. It is in the Museum Kunstpalast, Düsseldorf.

ordinary_time_17_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_17_tuesday.text: Landscape with the Parable of the Wheat and the Tares by Abraham Bloemaert, 1624. While the farmhands sleep, the devil slips through the field sowing weeds. It is in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.

ordinary_time_17_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_17_wednesday.text: The Parable of the Hidden Treasure, from the workshop of Rembrandt, about 1630, possibly painted with his first pupil Gerard Dou. A man digs by night in the field where the treasure lies. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest.

ordinary_time_18_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_18_tuesday.text: Christ at the Sea of Galilee, from the circle of Tintoretto, about 1575. Christ stands on the shore of the storm-tossed sea as Peter climbs over the side of the boat toward him. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

ordinary_time_20_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_20_wednesday.text: The Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard by Rembrandt, 1637. At day's end the landowner pays the workers in a dim barn, while those who worked all day complain. It is in the Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.

ordinary_time_21_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_21_thursday.text: The Wise and Foolish Virgins by Wilhelm von Schadow, 1838–42, a leader of the German Nazarene painters. Christ the bridegroom welcomes the wise virgins with their lamps lit, while the foolish ones arrive too late. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.

ordinary_time_22_tuesday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_22_tuesday.text: The Healings of Christ, an engraving from a series of Bible scenes, showing the cures at Capernaum. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_22_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_22_wednesday.text: Christ Healing the Mother of Simon Peter's Wife by John Bridges, 1839, an English painter. Christ takes the sick woman by the hand as the family watches.

ordinary_time_22_thursday.label: The cartoon
ordinary_time_22_thursday.text: The Miraculous Draught of Fishes by Raphael, 1515–16, a full-size design for a tapestry for the Sistine Chapel. Peter kneels in the overloaded boat: 'Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.' It is lent by the King to the Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

ordinary_time_22_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_22_saturday.text: Christ Defends the Plucking of the Grain on the Sabbath by Marten van Valckenborch, about 1580–90, the August picture in his series of the months. Harvesters work the wheat fields while Christ, walking through them with his disciples, answers the Pharisees. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

ordinary_time_23_monday.label: The illumination
ordinary_time_23_monday.text: The Healing of the Man with the Withered Hand, from the Hitda Codex, about 1000–20, painted in Cologne for Abbess Hitda of Meschede. Christ stretches out his hand toward the man across a blue sea of figures. It is in the University and State Library, Darmstadt.

ordinary_time_23_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_23_friday.text: The Parable of the Blind by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1568. Six blind men, holding on to each other, stumble one after another toward the ditch. It is in the Museo di Capodimonte, Naples.

ordinary_time_23_saturday.label: The print
ordinary_time_23_saturday.text: The House on the Rock, a 17th-century Dutch engraving from a series of 24 scenes from the New Testament. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_24_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_24_saturday.text: The Sower by Jean-François Millet, 1850. A peasant strides down a dark hillside flinging seed, while crows follow. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and later inspired Van Gogh.

ordinary_time_25_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_25_friday.text: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1612–14. The risen Christ, his wounds still showing, places the keys of the kingdom in Peter's hands. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

ordinary_time_25_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_25_saturday.text: Christ Carrying the Cross by El Greco, about 1577–87. Christ embraces the cross, his eyes raised to heaven. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_28_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_28_tuesday.text: The Dinner at the House of the Pharisee by Maria Felice Tibaldi Subleyras, about 1737, a small copy in miniature of her husband Pierre Subleyras's great canvas. It is in the Galleria Sabauda, Turin.

ordinary_time_29_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_29_thursday.text: Pentecost by Jean Restout, 1732. Tongues of fire descend on the apostles gathered around Mary. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

ordinary_time_30_monday.label: The print
ordinary_time_30_monday.text: Christ Lays His Hand on the Bent Woman, a 17th-century Dutch engraving. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_30_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_30_tuesday.text: Woman Baking Bread by Jean-François Millet, 1854. A peasant woman slides the loaves into the oven — the yeast she mixed into the flour has done its work. It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, the Netherlands.

ordinary_time_30_wednesday.label: The icon
ordinary_time_30_wednesday.text: The Ladder of Divine Ascent, a 12th-century icon at Saint Catherine's Monastery on Mount Sinai. Monks climb the rungs toward Christ, who reaches down to welcome the first; angels look on, while demons pull others off with hooks and ropes.

ordinary_time_30_friday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_30_friday.text: Christ Heals a Man with Dropsy at the House of a Pharisee, an 18th-century engraving. It is in the Wellcome Collection, London.

ordinary_time_30_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_30_saturday.text: The Peasant Wedding by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, about 1567. Guests crowd a barn for a wedding feast; the bride sits under a paper crown. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

ordinary_time_31_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_31_friday.text: The Parable of the Unjust Steward, after Marinus van Reymerswaele, 16th century, the Flemish painter of tax collectors and moneylenders. The steward rewrites the debtors' bills at his desk.

ordinary_time_31_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_31_saturday.text: The Moneylender and his Wife by Quentin Matsys, 1514. As he weighs gold, his wife turns from her prayer book to watch the coins — God or mammon. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

ordinary_time_32_saturday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_32_saturday.text: The Unjust Judge, a wood engraving after John Everett Millais from The Parables of Our Lord, 1864. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_33_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_33_thursday.text: Flevit super illam ('He Wept over It') by Enrique Simonet, 1892. From the Mount of Olives, Christ weeps as he looks across at the Temple and the walls of Jerusalem. It is in the Museo del Prado collection, on loan to the Museum of Málaga.

ordinary_time_33_friday.label: The etching
ordinary_time_33_friday.text: Christ Driving the Money Changers from the Temple, a Dutch print after a design by Jacob Jordaens, made between 1652 and 1702. Christ raises a whip of cords as the traders flee and the cattle stampede. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_33_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_33_saturday.text: Christ Teaching in the Temple by Christian Wilhelm Ernst Dietrich, 18th century, a German painter who worked in the manner of Rembrandt.

ordinary_time_34_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_34_friday.text: The Great Day of His Wrath by John Martin, 1851–53, the first of three vast paintings of the Last Judgment. Mountains collapse and a city tumbles into the abyss — 'heaven and earth will pass away.' It is in Tate Britain, London.

ordinary_time_34_saturday.label: The altarpiece
ordinary_time_34_saturday.text: The Last Judgment by Rogier van der Weyden, 1445–50, painted for the hospital of Beaune in Burgundy so that the sick could see it from their beds. St. Michael weighs souls beneath Christ in judgment. It is still in the Hôtel-Dieu, Beaune.

friday_after_ash_wednesday.label: The painting
friday_after_ash_wednesday.text: The Fight Between Carnival and Lent by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1559. In a crowded Flemish square, fat Carnival astride a barrel jousts with gaunt Lent, whose lance is a baker's paddle holding two herrings; half the town feasts, the other half fasts, prays and gives alms. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

saturday_after_ash_wednesday.label: The painting
saturday_after_ash_wednesday.text: The Calling of Saint Matthew, after Jan Sanders van Hemessen, 16th century. Levi, among his ledgers and coins, looks up as Christ calls him. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

lent_1_monday.label: The painting
lent_1_monday.text: The Last Judgment by Stefan Lochner, about 1435, the great painter of Cologne. Christ judges from a rainbow; on the left the saved are led by angels into a Gothic heaven, on the right devils drag the damned to hell. It is in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum, Cologne.

lent_1_tuesday.label: The print
lent_1_tuesday.text: Christ Teaching the Apostles the Lord's Prayer, a 16th-century German engraving by Hans Brosamer. It is in the collection of the Leiden University Library.

lent_1_saturday.label: The painting
lent_1_saturday.text: Landscape with the Good Samaritan by Rembrandt, 1638 — love for one's enemy. The tiny figure of the Samaritan leads the wounded man to the inn under a stormy sky. It is in the Czartoryski Museum, Kraków.

lent_2_thursday.label: The painting
lent_2_thursday.text: The Rich Man and Lazarus by Luca Giordano, 17th century. The poor man lies at the gate while the rich man feasts. It is in the Harvard Art Museums, Cambridge, Massachusetts.

lent_2_friday.label: The painting
lent_2_friday.text: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants by Domenico Fetti, about 1618–22, from his series of small paintings of the parables. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Dresden.

lent_3_tuesday.label: The painting
lent_3_tuesday.text: The Parable of the Unmerciful Servant by Jan Sanders van Hemessen, about 1556. The king's steward reads out the huge debt while the servant begs for time. It is in the University of Michigan Museum of Art, Ann Arbor.

lent_3_friday.label: The painting
lent_3_friday.text: The Good Samaritan (after Delacroix) by Vincent van Gogh, 1890, painted at Saint-Rémy from a print of Delacroix's picture — 'love your neighbor as yourself.' It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, the Netherlands.

lent_3_saturday.label: The painting
lent_3_saturday.text: Church Interior with the Pharisee and the Publican by Dirck van Delen, 17th century. In a vast imaginary church, the Pharisee stands boldly in front while the tax collector hangs back at the edge. It is in the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown, Massachusetts.

lent_4_wednesday.label: The fresco
lent_4_wednesday.text: The Holy Trinity by Masaccio, about 1427, one of the first paintings to use true perspective. The Father holds up the cross of the Son, and the dove of the Spirit passes between them. It is in Santa Maria Novella, Florence.

lent_4_thursday.label: The painting
lent_4_thursday.text: Moses with the Ten Commandments by Rembrandt, 1659. Moses raises the tablets of the Law above his head — 'he wrote about me.' It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

lent_4_friday.label: The drawing
lent_4_friday.text: Christ Preaching to the Elders in the Temple by John Martin, 19th century. It is in the Yale Center for British Art, New Haven.

lent_4_saturday.label: The painting
lent_4_saturday.text: Christ Instructing Nicodemus by Jacob Jordaens, about 1650. It is in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts, Brussels.

lent_5_monday.label: The painting
lent_5_monday.text: The Woman Taken in Adultery by Rembrandt, 1644. In the vast golden Temple, the woman kneels in white before Christ while her accusers press around. It is in the National Gallery, London.

lent_5_tuesday.label: The painting
lent_5_tuesday.text: The Crucifixion by Andrea Mantegna, 1457–59, from the predella of the San Zeno altarpiece in Verona. 'When you lift up the Son of Man.' It is in the Louvre, Paris.

lent_5_saturday.label: The painting
lent_5_saturday.text: Christ before the High Priest by Gerard van Honthorst, about 1617. Lit by a single candle, the high priest raises his finger as Christ stands calmly before him. It is in the National Gallery, London.

holy_monday.label: The painting
holy_monday.text: Mary Anointing the Feet of Christ by the Master of Perea, a late 15th-century Spanish painter from Valencia. It is in the Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven.

easter_time_2_tuesday.label: The painting
easter_time_2_tuesday.text: The Brazen Serpent by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1635–40. Moses lifts up the bronze serpent and the dying Israelites who look at it are healed — Christ's own image for his cross. It is in the National Gallery, London.

easter_time_2_saturday.label: The painting
easter_time_2_saturday.text: Walking on the Water by Ivan Aivazovsky, 1888, the great Russian painter of the sea. Christ walks toward the boat across a moonlit, storm-churned sea. It is in the Museum of the History of Religion, St. Petersburg.

easter_time_3_thursday.label: The painting
easter_time_3_thursday.text: The Last Supper by Tintoretto, 1592–94, his last great work. Christ gives the bread to the apostles in a dark inn lit by his own halo and by ghostly angels. It is in San Giorgio Maggiore, Venice.

easter_time_3_friday.label: The altarpiece
easter_time_3_friday.text: The Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the central panel of the Ghent Altarpiece by Hubert and Jan van Eyck, completed 1432. The Lamb of God stands on an altar, his blood flowing into a chalice, worshiped by saints from the four corners of the world. It is in St. Bavo's Cathedral, Ghent.

easter_time_3_saturday.label: The painting
easter_time_3_saturday.text: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1614. 'Master, to whom shall we go?' It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

easter_time_4_tuesday.label: The painting
easter_time_4_tuesday.text: The Good Shepherd by Bernhard Plockhorst, a German painter, about 1880, one of the most reproduced religious pictures of its time. Christ carries a lamb and leads the flock across a stream.

easter_time_4_thursday.label: The painting
easter_time_4_thursday.text: Jesus Washing Peter's Feet by Ford Madox Brown, 1852–56. Christ kneels with the towel as Peter, embarrassed, draws back his foot. It is in Tate Britain, London.

easter_time_5_monday.label: The painting
easter_time_5_monday.text: Pentecost by Titian, about 1555. The Spirit descends on Mary and the apostles under a great coffered vault. It is in Santa Maria della Salute, Venice.

easter_time_6_wednesday.label: The mosaic
easter_time_6_wednesday.text: Pentecost, an 11th-century mosaic in the monastery of Hosios Loukas, Greece. Rays from the dome descend on the apostles, seated in a circle.

easter_time_6_saturday.label: The painting
easter_time_6_saturday.text: Christ in Gethsemane by Heinrich Hofmann, 1890. It is in the Riverside Church, New York.

ordinary_time_4_monday.label: The print
ordinary_time_4_monday.text: Christ Heals the Possessed Man in the Region of the Gerasenes, a 17th-century Dutch print; the swine rush down the slope into the sea. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_4_thursday.label: The sculpture
ordinary_time_4_thursday.text: The Mission of the Apostles, the great tympanum over the central door of the Basilica of Vézelay in Burgundy, carved about 1130. Rays from Christ's hands fall on the apostles, sent to every people of the earth.

ordinary_time_14_wednesday.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_14_wednesday.text: The Sending of the Apostles, an 18th-century ceiling fresco in the monastery church of Nová Říše in Moravia.

ordinary_time_14_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_14_thursday.text: The Mission of the Apostles, 1631, in the Chapel of Saint Matthias in the Basilica of Santa Giustina, Padua.

ordinary_time_25_wednesday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_25_wednesday.text: Christ Sends Out the Twelve Apostles, a 16th-century Netherlandish engraving. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_20_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_20_tuesday.text: Christ and the Rich Young Man by Andrey Mironov, a contemporary Russian painter of Gospel scenes who shares his work freely. The young man turns away, and Jesus tells his disciples how hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom.

ordinary_time_23_tuesday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_23_tuesday.text: Christ Chooses His Apostles, an engraving from the Emblemata Novi Testamenti, a 17th-century Flemish picture book of the Gospels. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_27_friday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_27_friday.text: Christ Heals a Possessed Man before the Pharisees and Scribes, a 16th-century Netherlandish engraving. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_28_wednesday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_28_wednesday.text: Christ Speaks to the Scribes and Pharisees, an engraving in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_22_monday.label: The drawing
ordinary_time_22_monday.text: Christ in the Synagogue at Nazareth, a drawing from a series on the life of Christ. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

lent_3_monday.label: The engraving
lent_3_monday.text: The People of Nazareth Drive Christ out of the Town, a 17th-century engraving made for the Gospel of this very day, the Monday of the third week of Lent. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_32_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_32_monday.text: The Return of the Prodigal Son by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, 1667–70 — forgiveness without limit. The father embraces his ragged son while servants bring a robe and a ring and lead in the fatted calf. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

easter_time_3_monday.label: The painting
easter_time_3_monday.text: Christ Preaching at Capernaum by Maurycy Gottlieb, 1878–79, left unfinished when the young Polish-Jewish painter died at 23. Christ, in a prayer shawl, teaches in the synagogue. It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.

easter_time_3_wednesday.label: The painting
easter_time_3_wednesday.text: The Institution of the Eucharist by Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo, 1753, painted when he was in his twenties. Seated among the apostles, Christ gives them the bread that is his body. It is in the National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen.

easter_time_6_tuesday.label: The painting
easter_time_6_tuesday.text: The Ascension by Rembrandt, 1636, one of his Passion series for the Prince of Orange. Christ rises in a blaze of light on a cloud borne by cherubs. It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.

easter_time_6_thursday.label: The panels
easter_time_6_thursday.text: Christ Taking Leave of the Apostles, two panels by Duccio from the back of his Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral, 1308–11. At the Last Supper Christ tells them, 'A little while and you will no longer see me.' It is in the Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Siena.

easter_time_6_friday.label: The painting
easter_time_6_friday.text: The Nativity at Night by Geertgen tot Sint Jans, about 1490 — the grief of labor turned to joy. The newborn Child is the only source of light in the dark stable. It is in the National Gallery, London.

easter_time_7_tuesday.label: The painting
easter_time_7_tuesday.text: The Agony in the Garden by El Greco and his workshop, 1590s. Christ kneels in prayer on the Mount of Olives as an angel brings the cup, while the apostles sleep in a hollow of rock below. It is in the National Gallery, London.

ordinary_time_15_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_15_saturday.text: Christ Healing the Sick by Washington Allston, 1813, the first great American painter of Bible scenes. It is in the Worcester Art Museum, Massachusetts.

advent_1_tuesday.label: The fresco
advent_1_tuesday.text: The Prophet Isaiah by Michelangelo, 1508–12, on the Sistine Chapel ceiling — one of the prophets who longed to see what the disciples saw. He turns from his book as if called by the angel at his shoulder.

advent_3_thursday.label: The painting
advent_3_thursday.text: The Appearance of Christ Before the People by Alexander Ivanov, 1837–57, a canvas more than seven meters wide that took him twenty years. John the Baptist points to the distant figure of Christ: 'Prepare the way of the Lord.' It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

advent_december_24.label: The painting
advent_december_24.text: The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds by Thomas Cole, 1833–34, founder of the Hudson River School. The angel's light breaks over a vast moonlit landscape. It is in the Chrysler Museum of Art, Norfolk, Virginia.

ordinary_time_1_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_1_monday.text: The Calling of Peter and Andrew by Duccio, 1308–11, a panel from the back of his great Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

ordinary_time_1_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_1_friday.text: Christ Healing the Paralytic by Anthony van Dyck and his workshop, about 1621. 'Rise, take up your mat, and walk.'

ordinary_time_2_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_2_monday.text: The Wedding at Cana by Paolo Veronese, 1562–63, the largest painting in the Louvre. Napoleon's troops took it from the refectory of San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice; it now faces the Mona Lisa.

ordinary_time_3_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_3_saturday.text: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee by Rembrandt, 1633, his only seascape. It was stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston in 1990 and has never been found; its empty frame still hangs there.

ordinary_time_10_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_10_monday.text: The Sermon on the Mount by Jan Brueghel the Elder, 1598, painted on copper. A huge crowd in Flemish dress gathers on a hillside to hear Christ. It is in the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles.

ordinary_time_11_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_11_tuesday.text: The Good Samaritan by Théodule Ribot, 1870, a French realist known for his dark, Spanish-inspired style. It is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Pau.

easter_time_2_thursday.label: The icon
easter_time_2_thursday.text: Christ Pantocrator from St. Catherine's Monastery, Sinai, painted in wax in the 500s, one of the oldest icons in the world. The two sides of the face differ, showing Christ as both judge and merciful savior.

easter_time_2_friday.label: The painting
easter_time_2_friday.text: The Multiplication of the Loaves and Fishes by Paolo Farinati, in the church of San Giorgio in Braida, Verona. Five loaves and two fish feed five thousand.

easter_time_4_monday.label: The mosaic
easter_time_4_monday.text: The Good Shepherd, a mosaic of about 425–450 in the Mausoleum of Galla Placidia, Ravenna, one of the oldest and best-preserved Christian mosaics. A young, golden-robed Christ sits among his sheep beneath a deep blue vault of stars. 'I am the good shepherd.'

easter_time_5_tuesday.label: The painting
easter_time_5_tuesday.text: Christ Appearing to the Apostles after the Resurrection by Szymon Czechowicz, an 18th-century Polish painter trained in Rome. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.

lent_1_thursday.label: The painting
lent_1_thursday.text: The Light of the World by William Holman Hunt, 1851–53, the first version of the picture. Crowned with thorns and carrying a lantern, Christ knocks at an overgrown door that has no handle on the outside: 'Behold, I stand at the door and knock.' It hangs at Keble College, Oxford.

lent_1_friday.label: The painting
lent_1_friday.text: Cain Slaying Abel by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1608–09. Cain stands over his brother, about to strike, beside the smoking altar of their offerings: 'whoever is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment.' It is in the Courtauld Gallery, London.

lent_2_wednesday.label: The painting
lent_2_wednesday.text: The Agony in the Garden by Giovanni Bellini, about 1458–60. Christ prays on a rock as dawn breaks and the disciples sleep; Judas and the soldiers are already on their way. It is in the National Gallery, London.

thursday_after_ash_wednesday.label: The painting
thursday_after_ash_wednesday.text: Christ Carrying the Cross by Titian, about 1565. Simon of Cyrene leans in to share the weight as Christ turns his face toward us. It is in the Prado, Madrid.

lent_1_wednesday.label: The fresco
lent_1_wednesday.text: The prophet Jonah by Michelangelo, painted about 1511 on the Sistine Chapel ceiling, directly above the altar. He leans back to look up at God, the great fish behind him; his three days in its belly became the 'sign of Jonah', a sign of the Resurrection.

lent_2_monday.label: The painting
lent_2_monday.text: The Seven Acts of Mercy by Pieter Brueghel the Younger, early 1600s, one of several versions he painted. In a single village street the hungry are fed, the thirsty given drink, strangers taken in, the naked clothed, the sick and the prisoners visited, and the dead buried.

lent_2_tuesday.label: The painting
lent_2_tuesday.text: Christ Washing the Feet of the Disciples by Jacopo Tintoretto, about 1575–80. Christ kneels to wash Peter's feet while the others look on: the greatest among them as their servant. It is in the National Gallery, London.

lent_3_wednesday.label: The painting
lent_3_wednesday.text: Christ among the Doctors by Albrecht Dürer, 1506, painted in Venice in five days, as the note tucked into the book at the left says. Old teachers of the Law crowd around the boy Jesus with their books. It is in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.

lent_3_thursday.label: The watercolor
lent_3_thursday.text: Jesus Heals a Mute Possessed Man by James Tissot, 1886–94, one of the hundreds of watercolors of his Life of Christ, made after his journeys to the Holy Land. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.

lent_4_monday.label: The miniature
lent_4_monday.text: Jesus Heals the Nobleman's Son, a Mughal painting from a Mirror of Holiness, the life of Christ the Jesuit Jerome Xavier wrote in Persian for the emperor Akbar, illustrated at Allahabad, India, about 1602–04. It is in the Cleveland Museum of Art.

lent_4_tuesday.label: The painting
lent_4_tuesday.text: Christ Healing the Paralytic at the Pool of Bethesda by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, 1667–70, painted for the Hospital de la Caridad in Seville. The man who has waited thirty-eight years looks up as Christ tells him to rise. It is in the National Gallery, London.

lent_5_wednesday.label: The painting
lent_5_wednesday.text: 'What Is Truth?' Christ and Pilate, by Nikolai Ge, 1890. Pilate, in full sunlight, turns away with his question; Christ stands silent in the shadow. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

lent_5_thursday.label: The watercolor
lent_5_thursday.text: The Jews Took Up Rocks to Stone Jesus by James Tissot, 1886–96, from his Life of Christ. The crowd snatches up stones from the Temple works as Christ slips away. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.

lent_5_friday.label: The watercolor
lent_5_friday.text: Jesus Walks in the Portico of Solomon by James Tissot, 1886–94, from his Life of Christ: the Temple colonnade where this argument took place, in winter, at the feast of the Dedication. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.

advent_december_21.label: The painting
advent_december_21.text: The Visitation by Rogier van der Weyden, about 1435–40. Mary and Elizabeth, both expecting, meet on a path in the Flemish countryside, each resting a hand on the other. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Leipzig.

advent_december_23.label: The painting
advent_december_23.text: The Naming of John the Baptist by Fra Angelico, about 1435. Zechariah, still unable to speak, writes 'His name is John' while Elizabeth's household looks on. It is in the Museo di San Marco, Florence.

christmas_octave_day_5.label: The painting
christmas_octave_day_5.text: Simeon's Song of Praise by Rembrandt, 1631. In a vast, dim temple one shaft of light falls on old Simeon holding the Child, with Mary and Joseph kneeling beside him. It is in the Mauritshuis, The Hague.

christmas_octave_day_7.label: The painting
christmas_octave_day_7.text: The Holy Night by Correggio, about 1528–30, one of the first paintings in which all the light comes from the newborn Child. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

lent_2_saturday.label: The painting
lent_2_saturday.text: The Return of the Prodigal Son by Rembrandt, about 1668, painted near the end of his life. The ragged son kneels with his head against his father's chest, and the father's two hands rest on his back. It is in the Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.

ordinary_time_33_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_33_monday.text: Christ Healing the Blind of Jericho by Nicolas Poussin, 1650. On the road outside the city, Christ touches the eyes of one blind man while the other gropes his way forward. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

ordinary_time_33_wednesday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_33_wednesday.text: The Return of the Lord, from a series of six engravings on the parable of the talents made in 1565 by Harmen Jansz. Muller after Maarten van Heemskerck. The master comes home to settle accounts with his servants. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_34_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_34_monday.text: The Widow's Mite by the French painter Émile Auguste Hublin (1830–1891). A poor widow drops her two small coins into the Temple treasury. It is in the Herbert Art Gallery and Museum, Coventry.

ordinary_time_34_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_34_wednesday.text: The Christian Martyrs' Last Prayer by Jean-Léon Gérôme, commissioned in 1863 and finished twenty years later. In a Roman arena a group of Christians kneel together in prayer as a lion steps out of its cage. It is in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.

ordinary_time_34_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_34_thursday.text: The Destruction of the Temple of Jerusalem by Francesco Hayez, 1867. Roman soldiers storm the Temple in AD 70 as the city burns, the fall Jesus foretold. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.

advent_1_friday.label: The painting
advent_1_friday.text: Christ Healing the Blind by El Greco, about 1570, painted in Italy before he settled in Spain. Christ touches the eyes of a kneeling blind man while the crowd argues around them. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

advent_2_wednesday.label: The painting
advent_2_wednesday.text: Christus Consolator ('Christ the Comforter') by Ary Scheffer, 1851. The weary, the grieving, the captive and the oppressed gather around Christ, who looks up to heaven.

advent_2_thursday.label: The painting
advent_2_thursday.text: Saint John the Baptist in the Wilderness by Caravaggio, about 1604. The prophet sits alone in the dark, wrapped in a red cloak, his reed cross beside him. It is in the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.

advent_2_friday.label: The painting
advent_2_friday.text: Children's Games by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1560. A whole town square is taken over by children playing some eighty different games, like the children in the market place Jesus describes. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

wednesday_after_epiphany.label: The painting
wednesday_after_epiphany.text: The Disciples See Christ Walking on the Water by Henry Ossawa Tanner, about 1907. From their boat in the night the disciples make out a figure of light coming toward them across the sea. It is in the Des Moines Art Center.

thursday_after_epiphany.label: The painting
thursday_after_epiphany.text: Jesus in the Synagogue by the Danish painter Joakim Skovgaard, 1914, a study for his altarpiece in Herning Church in Jutland. Jesus stands with the scroll of Isaiah before the people of Nazareth.

ordinary_time_1_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_1_wednesday.text: On the Sea of Galilee by Vasily Polenov, 1888, one of the paintings from his long journey through Palestine. Christ walks alone along the shore of the lake, deep in thought. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

ordinary_time_2_wednesday.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_2_wednesday.text: The Healing of the Man with the Withered Hand, a fresco in the Chapel of the Holy Trinity at Lublin Castle, Poland, finished in 1418. Painters from Ruthenia covered the Gothic chapel in Byzantine-style frescoes for King Władysław II Jagiełło.

ordinary_time_2_friday.label: The icon
ordinary_time_2_friday.text: The Synaxis of the Twelve Apostles, an icon painted in Constantinople in the early 1300s. The twelve stand together in two rows, with Peter and Paul at the front. It is in the Pushkin Museum, Moscow.

ordinary_time_2_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_2_saturday.text: Christ Preaching to the Multitudes by the English painter James Smetham (1821–1889), a friend of Rossetti and Ruskin. The crowd presses so close around Jesus that there is hardly room to move.

ordinary_time_3_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_3_wednesday.text: Landscape with the Parable of the Sower by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1557. A sower scatters seed in the foreground while birds wait behind him and the river valley opens beyond. It is in the Timken Museum of Art, San Diego.

ordinary_time_4_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_4_wednesday.text: Christ in the House of His Parents ('The Carpenter's Shop') by John Everett Millais, 1849–50. In Joseph's workshop the boy Jesus has cut his palm on a nail, and Mary kneels to comfort him. It is in Tate Britain, London.

ordinary_time_5_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_5_monday.text: Jesus Teaching on the Seashore by James Tissot, one of some 350 watercolors of the life of Christ he painted between 1886 and 1894 after travels in the Holy Land. The people of the lakeside towns crowd down to the water to see him. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.

easter_time_3_tuesday.label: The painting
easter_time_3_tuesday.text: The Israelites Gathering Manna in the Desert by Nicolas Poussin, 1637–39. The starving people fall on the bread from heaven, while Moses points upward to the God who sent it. It is in the Louvre, Paris.

easter_time_4_wednesday.label: The painting
easter_time_4_wednesday.text: Christ as 'The Light of the World' by Paris Bordone, the Venetian painter who trained with Titian. It is in the National Gallery, London.

easter_time_4_friday.label: The painting
easter_time_4_friday.text: The Last Supper by Girolamo Muziano, painted on copper in late 16th-century Rome. The apostles crowd around the table on the night Jesus told them, 'I am the way, and the truth, and the life.' It is in the National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen.

easter_time_4_saturday.label: The painting
easter_time_4_saturday.text: The Holy Trinity by El Greco, 1577–79, painted for the high altar of the monastery of Santo Domingo el Antiguo in Toledo. God the Father holds the body of his Son, with the Holy Spirit as a dove above them. It is in the Prado, Madrid.

easter_time_5_wednesday.label: The icon
easter_time_5_wednesday.text: Christ the Vine, an icon attributed to the workshop of the painter Theophanes, late 1500s or early 1600s. Christ sits at the heart of the vine holding an open Gospel, and its branches carry the twelve apostles. It is in the Byzantine and Christian Museum, Athens.

easter_time_5_friday.label: The fresco
easter_time_5_friday.text: The Last Supper by Andrea del Castagno, about 1447, on the refectory wall of the convent of Sant'Apollonia in Florence. Christ sits among his friends in a marble-panelled room, with Judas alone on the near side of the table.

easter_time_5_saturday.label: The fresco
easter_time_5_saturday.text: The Mocking of Christ by Fra Angelico, about 1440, painted in a friar's cell at San Marco in Florence. Christ sits blindfolded while hands strike him, and Mary and Saint Dominic keep watch in front.

easter_time_7_monday.label: The painting
easter_time_7_monday.text: The Agony in the Garden by Andrea Mantegna, about 1455. Christ prays on a rock while his disciples sleep, and Judas leads the soldiers out of Jerusalem toward them. It is in the National Gallery, London.

easter_time_7_wednesday.label: The fresco
easter_time_7_wednesday.text: The Last Supper by Giotto, about 1305, in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. The apostles sit around the table in a simple room, John leaning on Jesus' breast.

easter_time_7_thursday.label: The fresco
easter_time_7_thursday.text: The Last Supper by Domenico Ghirlandaio and his brother Davide, 1476, in the refectory of the abbey of Passignano in Tuscany. The apostles sit along one side of a long white table, with Judas alone in front.

easter_time_7_saturday.label: The painting
easter_time_7_saturday.text: Saint John the Evangelist on Patmos by Titian and his workshop, about 1553–55, painted for a ceiling in Venice and meant to be seen from below. The beloved disciple looks up into the heavens as an eagle spreads its wings beside him. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

ordinary_time_7_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_7_tuesday.text: Suffer the Little Children to Come unto Me by Fritz von Uhde, 1884. Christ sits in a plain room of the artist's own day, and shy village children come up to him. It is in the Museum der bildenden Künste, Leipzig.

ordinary_time_7_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_7_thursday.text: Giving Drink to the Thirsty, one panel of the Seven Works of Mercy by the Master of Alkmaar, 1504. Townspeople fill the cups of beggars and cripples while Christ stands among the poor. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_7_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_7_friday.text: Adam and Eve by Lucas Cranach the Elder, 1526. The first man and woman stand together in the garden among the animals of creation. It is in the Courtauld Gallery, London.

ordinary_time_7_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_7_saturday.text: Christ Blessing the Children by Lucas Cranach the Younger and his workshop, about 1545. Mothers press forward with their babies as Christ lays his hands on them. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_8_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_8_tuesday.text: The Calling of Saints Peter and Andrew, attributed to Caravaggio, about 1603–06. Christ calls the two fishermen brothers away from their work. It is in the Royal Collection, at Hampton Court Palace.

ordinary_time_8_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_8_thursday.text: Christ Healing the Blind by El Greco, about 1570, painted in Italy before he settled in Spain. Christ touches the eyes of the blind man in a deep piazza, as the crowd argues around them. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_8_saturday.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_8_saturday.text: The Expulsion of the Money-changers from the Temple by Giotto, about 1305, in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. The next day the priests and elders came to ask him by what authority he had done it.

ordinary_time_9_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_9_wednesday.text: Moses before the Burning Bush by Domenico Fetti. Moses kneels before the fire from which God speaks: 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.

ordinary_time_10_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_10_wednesday.text: Moses with the Ten Commandments by Philippe de Champaigne, about 1648. Moses holds up the two tablets of the law, with light streaming from his head.

ordinary_time_11_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_11_saturday.text: Saint Francis Preaching to the Birds, Johann Anton Ramboux's copy of the fresco in the Upper Church of San Francesco, Assisi. Francis speaks to the birds of the air, which neither sow nor reap, and yet God feeds them.

ordinary_time_12_tuesday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_12_tuesday.text: The Broad and the Narrow Way, the English edition (1883) of a German print first published in 1866. The wide road on the left runs past theaters and taverns to destruction; the narrow one climbs past church and Sunday school to the heavenly city. It is in the British Museum.

ordinary_time_13_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_13_wednesday.text: The Miracle of the Gadarene Swine, a page from a manuscript painted around the year 1000. The demons driven out of the men enter the herd of swine, which rush down into the sea.

ordinary_time_13_thursday.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_13_thursday.text: The Healing of the Paralytic at Capernaum by Belisario Corenzio, on the ceiling of the chapter room of the monastery of Santi Severino e Sossio in Naples, early 1600s.

ordinary_time_14_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_14_monday.text: The Raising of Jairus' Daughter by Vasily Polenov, 1871, the painting that won him the gold medal of the Imperial Academy of Arts in St. Petersburg. Christ reaches toward the girl on her bed as her mother kneels and the mourners wait in the shadows.

ordinary_time_14_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_14_tuesday.text: The Gleaners by Jean-François Millet, 1857. Three peasant women bend to pick up the ears of grain left behind, while the great harvest is gathered in the distance. It is in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

ordinary_time_14_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_14_friday.text: Saint Paul before King Agrippa by Hendrick Bloemaert, 1635. Paul, in red, makes his defense before the king, Bernice and the governor Festus, as Christ foretold: “you will be dragged before governors and kings for my sake.” It is in the Centraal Museum, Utrecht.

ordinary_time_15_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_15_tuesday.text: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah by John Martin, 1852. Fire falls from heaven on the two cities as Lot and his daughters flee and his wife turns back. It is in the Laing Art Gallery, Newcastle.

ordinary_time_15_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_15_friday.text: The Disciples Plucking Grain on the Sabbath, one of the 160 panels of the Gotha Altarpiece painted in Heinrich Füllmaurer's workshop about 1538. It is at Friedenstein Castle, Gotha.

ordinary_time_16_tuesday.label: The altarpiece
ordinary_time_16_tuesday.text: The Holy Kinship (the Torgau Altarpiece) by Lucas Cranach the Elder, 1509. Mary and her relatives gather with their children, among them the 'brethren of the Lord'. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.

ordinary_time_16_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_16_wednesday.text: September: the Parable of the Sower by Marten van Valckenborch, 1580s, from a series of the months set in the Flemish countryside.

ordinary_time_16_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_16_friday.text: The Sower by Vincent van Gogh, June 1888, painted at Arles. A sower strides across a violet field under a huge yellow sun, with ripe wheat behind him. It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, the Netherlands.

ordinary_time_16_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_16_saturday.text: The Parable of the Wheat and the Tares by Domenico Fetti, one of his small parable paintings made in Mantua around 1620. While everyone sleeps, the enemy sows weeds among the wheat. It is in the Courtauld Gallery, London.

ordinary_time_17_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_17_friday.text: The Childhood of Christ by Gerard van Honthorst, about 1620. By candlelight the boy Jesus holds the light for Joseph at his carpenter's bench. It is in the Hermitage, St. Petersburg.

ordinary_time_18_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_18_monday.text: The Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes by Jacopo Tintoretto, about 1545–50. The great crowd sits on the hillside as the bread and fish are handed out. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_18_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_18_thursday.text: Christ Giving the Keys of Heaven to Saint Peter by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1612–15. Peter kneels to receive the keys of the kingdom. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

ordinary_time_18_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_18_saturday.text: Christ Healing the Boy Possessed by a Demon, a panel of the Sherborne Almshouse Triptych, Flemish, about 1480–90. The father brings his son to Jesus, and beyond them the blind Bartimaeus is healed. It belongs to the Almshouse of Saint John in Sherborne, England.

ordinary_time_19_monday.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_19_monday.text: The Tribute Money by Masaccio, about 1425, in the Brancacci Chapel of Santa Maria del Carmine, Florence. In one fresco Peter is told to catch a fish, finds the coin in its mouth at the lakeside, and hands it to the tax collector.

ordinary_time_19_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_19_thursday.text: The Parable of the Unforgiving Servant by Claude Vignon, 1629: the servant who was forgiven a great debt but would not forgive a small one.

ordinary_time_19_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_19_friday.text: Adam and Eve by Albrecht Dürer, 1507, two panels painted after his second journey to Italy. 'From the beginning it was not so.' It is in the Prado, Madrid.

ordinary_time_20_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_20_monday.text: Saint Anthony Distributing His Wealth to the Poor by the Master of the Osservanza, about 1430–35. Hearing this very Gospel read in church, the young Anthony gave away everything he owned. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

ordinary_time_20_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_20_thursday.text: The Parable of the Royal Wedding by Pieter Aertsen, about 1570. The king's servants bring in guests from the streets to fill the wedding feast.

ordinary_time_21_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_21_monday.text: Woe unto You, Scribes and Pharisees by James Tissot, from his watercolors of the life of Christ, 1886–94. Jesus confronts the scribes and Pharisees in the Temple. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.

ordinary_time_21_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_21_wednesday.text: Absalom's Pillar, Valley of Jehoshaphat by David Roberts, 1839. The ancient tombs cut into the rock of the Kidron Valley, just outside the walls of Jerusalem. It is in the Cleveland Museum of Art.

ordinary_time_24_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_24_friday.text: Mary Magdalene by Carlo Crivelli, about 1480. She holds the jar of ointment, dressed in rich brocade. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_26_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_26_tuesday.text: Christ and His Disciples by the Flemish Master of the Prodigal Son, 1500s. Jesus walks with his disciples through the countryside.

ordinary_time_27_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_27_tuesday.text: Kitchen Scene with Christ in the House of Martha and Mary by Diego Velázquez, 1618, painted when he was nineteen. A sulking servant pounds garlic in the kitchen, while through a hatch Mary sits at Christ's feet. It is in the National Gallery, London.

ordinary_time_27_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_27_wednesday.text: The Lord's Prayer by James Tissot, from his watercolors of the life of Christ, 1886–94. Jesus sits among his disciples, teaching them to pray. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.

ordinary_time_27_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_27_saturday.text: The Lucca Madonna by Jan van Eyck, about 1437. Mary sits enthroned in a small room and nurses the Christ Child. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.

ordinary_time_28_monday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_28_monday.text: Seascape with Jonah and the Whale by Gaspard Dughet, about 1653–54. Lightning splits the sky over a storm-tossed sea as Jonah is thrown to the great fish. It is in the Royal Collection.

ordinary_time_28_thursday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_28_thursday.text: The Tomb of Absalom by Vasily Polenov, 1882, painted in the Kidron Valley below the walls of Jerusalem, among the old tombs of kings and prophets. It is in the Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts.

ordinary_time_28_saturday.label: The fresco
ordinary_time_28_saturday.text: Saint Stephen Preaching and Saint Stephen Addressing the Council by Fra Angelico, 1448–50, in the Niccoline Chapel of the Vatican. Stephen speaks, full of the Holy Spirit, first to the people and then to the council.

ordinary_time_29_wednesday.label: The engraving
ordinary_time_29_wednesday.text: The Servant Waiting at Night for His Master, an etching by Jan Luyken, 1712. A light burns as the servant stands ready by the door. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

ordinary_time_29_friday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_29_friday.text: Wheat Fields by Jacob van Ruisdael, about 1670. Great clouds build over the ripening Dutch fields. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

ordinary_time_29_saturday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_29_saturday.text: September: the Parable of the Barren Fig Tree by Abel Grimmer, from a series of the months. The owner comes looking for fruit and finds none, and the vinedresser begs for one more year.

ordinary_time_31_wednesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_31_wednesday.text: The Tower of Babel by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1563: a tower begun and never finished. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

ordinary_time_33_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_33_tuesday.text: Zacchaeus by the Danish painter Niels Larsen Stevns, 1913. Jesus meets the tax collector who climbed a tree to see him.

ordinary_time_34_tuesday.label: The painting
ordinary_time_34_tuesday.text: The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans under the Command of Titus, A.D. 70 by David Roberts, 1850. From the Mount of Olives the Roman army looks across at the burning city and its Temple.

advent_2_monday.label: The fresco
advent_2_monday.text: Christ Healing the Paralytic, a wall painting from the house-church at Dura-Europos in Syria, about AD 232, one of the oldest known pictures of Christ. The healed man walks away carrying his bed. It is in the Yale University Art Gallery.

advent_2_saturday.label: The painting
advent_2_saturday.text: Elijah in the Desert by Washington Allston, 1818. The prophet kneels in a barren landscape as the ravens bring him food. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
